**Al-Wahidi's commentary (al-Wajiz) on Surah 2, verse 1:**

﴿Alif Lam Mim﴾ — I am Allah, the All-Knowing.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 2:

﴿That is the Book﴾: i.e., this Book, meaning the Qur'an. ﴿There is no doubt in it﴾: i.e., there is no doubt in it, meaning it is true and correct. It was also said that its wording is that of a statement, but what is intended is a prohibition against doubting it. He said: ﴿So there shall be no obscenity, nor wickedness﴾ [2:197]. And there is no doubt in it that it is ﴿guidance﴾: clarification and direction, ﴿for the muttaqin﴾: for the believers who guard against shirk (ishrak). In His specifying His Book as guidance for the muttaqin there is an indication that it is not guidance for others, and He has said: ﴿And as for those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness﴾ [41:44].

﴿Those who believe in the unseen﴾: they affirm (yuṣaddiqūn) ﴿the unseen﴾: what is hidden from them, namely Paradise, the Fire, and the Resurrection. ﴿And establish the prayer﴾: they perform it constantly and guard it. ﴿And from what We have provided them﴾: what We have given them and from which they benefit. ﴿They spend﴾: they bring it out in obedience to Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 4:

﴿And those who believe in what has been sent down to you﴾ was revealed concerning the believers among the People of the Book, who believe in the Qur'an. ﴿And what was sent down before you﴾ means: the Torah. ﴿And in the Hereafter﴾ means: and in the Last Abode. ﴿They are certain﴾: they know it with certainty, through reasoned inference.

Those (who are) described by these attributes are ﴿upon guidance﴾, meaning clarity and insight, ﴿from their Lord﴾, meaning from the presence of their Lord, ﴿and those are the successful ones﴾, meaning those who remain in everlasting bliss.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 6:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 7:

Verse 2:8: "And among the people are those who say, 'We believe in Allah and the Last Day,' but they are not believers."

This was revealed concerning the hypocrites (al-munafiqun), who displayed the word of faith while concealing disbelief. Thus Allah, glorified is He, negated faith from them with His saying: "but they are not believers." This indicates that the reality of faith is not merely verbal affirmation.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 52:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 54:

﴿And when Moses said to his people﴾ — those who worshipped the calf — ﴿"O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf"﴾ — as a god — ﴿so turn in repentance to your Creator﴾ — i.e., your Creator (khaliq). Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 55:

﴿And when you said, "O Musa, we will never believe you until we see Allah openly."﴾ It means: those whom Musa (peace be upon him) had chosen to make apology to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for the worship of the calf. When they heard the speech of Allah, the Exalted, and Musa had finished his intimate conversation (munajah) with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, they said to him: ﴿"We will never believe you"﴾, meaning, "we will never accept what you say as true, ﴿until we see Allah openly﴾", that is, plainly, with nothing veiling Him from us. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized you﴾, and it is a fire that came down from the sky and burned them all, ﴿while you were looking on﴾ at it as it descended. The thunderbolt seized them only because they refused to believe in Musa (peace be upon him) after his miracle had appeared, until their Lord would show Himself to them openly. Belief in the prophets is obligatory once their miracles have manifested, and it is not permissible to propose miracles to them; for this reason Allah, the Exalted, punished them. This verse is a rebuke to them for opposing the Messenger (ﷺ) even though his miracle was established, just as their forefathers opposed Musa despite the manifest signs he brought.

Everything that is in a covering (ghilaf) is called aghlaf (wrapped), and its plural is ghulf. Then God, exalted is He, refuted them, saying: ﴿Rather, God has cursed them﴾, that is, He removed them far from His mercy and expelled them. ﴿So little is it that they believe﴾, that is, they believe with little of what is in their hands. Qatadah said: ﴿So little is it that they believe﴾ means that only a few of them believe, such as Abdullah ibn Salam.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 89:

﴿And when there came to them a Book﴾, meaning: the Qur'an, ﴿confirming﴾, agreeing with, ﴿what was with them﴾. ﴿And they had been﴾, meaning: the Jews, ﴿before﴾ the revelation of the Book, ﴿seeking victory﴾ (yastaftihuna), meaning: seeking help, ﴿over those who disbelieved﴾ in Muhammad (ﷺ) and his Book, saying: "O Allah, grant us victory through the Prophet who will be sent at the end of time." ﴿But when there came to them what they recognised﴾, meaning: the Book and the mission of the Prophet, ﴿they disbelieved﴾. Then he censured their conduct, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 90:

﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls﴾, i.e., wretched is what they sold the share of their souls of reward for, by disbelieving in the Qur'an, ﴿out of envy﴾, i.e., out of jealousy, ﴿that God should send down﴾, i.e., that God should send down ﴿of His bounty upon whomever He wills of His servants﴾. And that is because the disbelief of the Jews was not from doubt or confusion; rather it was from envy, since prophethood had come to be among the descendants of Isma'il (peace be upon him). ﴿So they returned﴾, i.e., they went back and bore ﴿wrath upon wrath﴾: ﴿wrath﴾ from God upon them because of their neglect of the Torah, ﴿upon wrath﴾ for their disbelief in the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 91:

﴿And when it is said﴾ to the Jews, ﴿"Believe in what Allah has sent down"﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿they say, "We believe in what was sent down to us"﴾. He means: the Torah. ﴿And they reject what is after it﴾ — what is other than it — ﴿while it is the truth﴾. He means: the Qur'an, ﴿confirming what is with them﴾, agreeing with the Torah. Then Allah, exalted is He, refuted them regarding their saying "We believe in what was sent down to us" by His words: ﴿Why then did you kill the prophets of Allah?﴾ That is: what Book permitted the killing of a prophet?! ﴿If you are believers﴾ — this is a conditional clause, and its answer is what precedes it. Then he mentioned that they disbelieved in Allah, exalted is He, despite the clarity of the signs in the time of Moses, peace be upon him, so he said:
﴿And Moses had certainly come to you with clear proofs﴾, meaning: the staff, the hand, and the splitting of the sea. ﴿Then you took the calf after him﴾ as a god, ﴿while you were wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 93:

﴿And when We took your covenant and raised above you the mount, [saying]: Take what We have given you with determination, and listen.﴾ Its tafsir has already passed. And the meaning of "listen" (wa-usma'u) is: accept what is in it of its lawful and unlawful things, and obey. ﴿They said: We have heard﴾ what is in it, ﴿and we disobey﴾ what we were commanded. ﴿And they were made to drink the calf into their hearts﴾: they were given the love of the calf to drink and it was mixed with them, the love of the calf being mixed into them until it permeated them; the meaning is that the calf was made beloved to them. ﴿Because of their disbelief﴾, through their belief in anthropomorphism, for they sought what could be imagined in their souls. ﴿Say: Evil is that which your faith commands you, if you are believers﴾. This is a refutation of them in their saying: "We believe in what was sent down to us." That is because their fathers claimed faith and then worshipped the calf, so it was said to them: evil is the faith that commands you to disbelief. The meaning is: if you were believers, you would not have worshipped the calf, meaning your fathers. Likewise, you, if you were believers in what was sent down to you, you would not have denied Muhammad.

Qur'an 2:94: "Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is yours exclusively, to the exclusion of other people, then wish for death, if you are truthful."

The Jews used to say: "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews (hūdan)." So it was said to them: "If you are truthful, then wish for death, for whoever has no doubt that he is going to Paradise, Paradise is preferable to him."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 95:

﴿And they will never wish for it, ever.﴾ Because they knew that they were disbelievers and that they had no share in Paradise. This is His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿because of what their hands have put forth.﴾ That is: because of what they did of concealing the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) and altering his description. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ In it is the meaning of a threat.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 96:

﴿And you will find them﴾, O Muhammad, meaning: the scholars of the Jews, ﴿the most eager of people for life﴾, because they knew that if they died they would be headed to the Fire on account of what they had done regarding the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And [more eager] than those who associate partners [with God]﴾, i.e., and more eager than those who deny the Resurrection. Whoever denies the Resurrection loves a long life, because he does not hope for a resurrection. The Jews are more eager than them, because they knew what they had committed, so they fear the Fire. ﴿Each one of them wishes﴾, i.e., each one of the Jews, ﴿that he might be granted a life of a thousand years﴾, because he knows that his Hereafter has been spoiled for him. ﴿And it is not﴾, i.e., none of them is, ﴿one to remove him﴾, i.e., to distance him, ﴿from the punishment by being granted long life﴾, meaning, by the granting of his long life.

The Jews asked the Prophet ﷺ about which angel comes to him. He said, "Jibril." They said, "He is our enemy. Even if Mika'il had come to you, we would have believed in you." So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibril...﴾. The meaning is: say, whoever is an enemy to Jibril, let him die of rage. ﴿For indeed he has brought it down﴾, that is, he brought down the Qur'an ﴿upon your heart, by the permission of Allah﴾, by the command of Allah, ﴿confirming﴾, agreeing with what came before it of the Books, ﴿and as guidance and good tidings for the believers﴾. This is a reply to the Jews when they said that Jibril descends with war and severity. It was said that although he does descend with war and severity upon the disbelievers, he descends with guidance and good tidings for the believers.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 98:

﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah, His angels, His messengers, Jibril and Mika'il—indeed, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers.﴾ That is: whoever is an enemy to any one of these, then Allah is an enemy to him, because the enemy of one is the enemy of all, and the enemy of Muhammad (ﷺ) is the enemy of Allah. The wāw here is in the sense of "or," like His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers﴾, because whoever disbelieves in one of them is a disbeliever in all of them. And His saying: ﴿indeed, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ means: He Himself undertook that enmity and was sufficient for His angels and messengers in the matter of whoever opposes them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 99:

﴿And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs﴾ — clear indications and evidences. This is a reply to Ibn Suriya when he said: "O Muhammad, bring us no clear sign that we might follow you by it." ﴿And none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾ — those who depart from their religions. The Jews, by their disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ), departed from the law of Musa (peace be upon him). When Muhammad (ﷺ) mentioned to them the covenant that God Most High had taken from them concerning him, Malik ibn al-Sayf said: "By God, no covenant or pledge was made to us concerning Muhammad." So God Most High revealed:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 100:

﴿Is it not that every time they make a covenant, a party of them casts it aside?﴾ and His words ﴿a party of them cast it aside﴾, meaning: those among their scholars who broke it. ﴿Rather, most of them do not believe﴾, because they are among those who break the covenant, or who deny his prophethood and oppose him stubbornly.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 101:

And His saying: ﴿A party of those who were given the Scripture threw away the Book of Allah﴾, meaning: the scholars of the Jews. ﴿The Book of Allah﴾ means the Torah. ﴿Behind their backs﴾, meaning: they abandoned acting upon it when they disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an. ﴿As if they did not know﴾ that it is true and that what he brought is the truth. This is a report about their obstinacy. Then he informed that they rejected the writing and followed magic, so he said: ﴿And they followed﴾, meaning: the scholars of the Jews.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 102:

﴿What the devils recited﴾, i.e., what the devils used to relate and narrate of magic ﴿during the reign of Solomon﴾, in his time and the period of his kingship. This is because when Solomon, peace be upon him, was deprived of his kingship, the devils buried magic and talismans (nayranjat) in his treasury. When Solomon died, the devils pointed the people to them until they extracted them, and they said to the people: "Solomon only ruled you by this, so learn it." The Children of Israel then busied themselves with learning it and abandoned the books of their prophets. Then God cleared Solomon, peace be upon him, and said: ﴿Solomon did not disbelieve﴾, i.e., he was not a disbeliever or a sorcerer who practiced magic, ﴿but the devils disbelieved﴾ in God, ﴿teaching people magic﴾, meaning: what the devils wrote for them of the books of magic ﴿and what was sent down to the two angels﴾, i.e., and they taught them what was sent down upon the two, i.e., what the two were taught, inspired, and cast into their hearts of the knowledge of distinction (ʿilm al-tafriqa), which is a charm (ruqya) and not magic. His saying ﴿and they do not teach anyone﴾, meaning: the two angels do not teach magic to ﴿anyone﴾, anyone at all, ﴿until they say: "We are only a trial"﴾, a test and an examination, ﴿so do not disbelieve﴾. This is because God, Mighty and Majestic, tested the people through the two angels at that time, and made the trial in disbelief and faith to be that the one who accepts learning magic disbelieves by learning it, and believes by abandoning it. God may test His servants with whatever He wills. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve﴾, i.e., a trial from God; we inform you that practicing magic is disbelief in God, and we forbid you from it. If you obey us you will be saved, and if you disobey us you will be destroyed. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and they learn﴾, i.e., they come and learn from the two angels ﴿what they use to cause separation between a man and his wife﴾, which is that each of them is taken away from the other and each is made hateful to the other. ﴿But they cannot harm anyone thereby﴾, i.e., the sorcerers who learn magic cannot harm anyone with magic ﴿except by the permission of God﴾, by His will and decree. That is, they do not harm anyone through magic except one whom God wills to be struck by that harm. ﴿And they learn what harms them﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿and does not benefit them﴾ (in this world). ﴿And they had certainly known﴾, meaning: the Jews, ﴿that whoever purchases it﴾, i.e., whoever chooses magic, ﴿would have no share in the Hereafter﴾, no portion in Paradise. Then He censured their conduct, saying: ﴿And wretched is that for which they sold themselves﴾, i.e., how evil is the thing for which they sold their own portion, in choosing magic and casting away the Book of God ﴿if only they had known﴾ the reality of what awaits those who forfeit the Hereafter of punishment.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 103:

﴿And if only they had believed﴾ in Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Qur'an, ﴿and had feared Allah﴾ by abandoning Judaism and magic, they would have been rewarded with something better for them than what they earned through magic, and this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, a reward from Allah would have been better, if they only knew.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 104:

﴿O you who have believed, do not say, "Ra'ina,"﴾ The Muslims used to say to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Ra'ina sam'aka" (meaning "Pay attention to us," or "Listen to us"). In the language of the Jews, however, this was a foul insult. When they heard this word that they were saying to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it pleased them. So they would come to him, say that, and laugh among themselves. Allah the Exalted forbade the believers from this, and revealed this verse, and commanded them to say instead of "Ra'ina," ﴿"Unzurna,"﴾ that is: "Look upon us," so that we may make you understand what we are saying. ﴿"And listen"﴾ that is: obey, and leave off this word, because obedience is required by hearing. ﴿Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture, nor the polytheists, would not like that there be sent down to you any good from your Lord.﴾ That is: any good from your Lord.

The commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 105:

﴿Wa-llahu yakhtassu bi-rahmatihi﴾ (And Allah singles out for His mercy) — He specifies with His prophethood ﴿man yasha'u﴾ (whom He wills), ﴿wa-llahu dhu al-fadli al-'azim﴾ (and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 106:

﴿Whatever abrogation We cause of a verse, or cause it to be forgotten﴾, meaning: We do not remove a verse by way of abrogation, either by annulling its ruling (naskh) or by causing it to be forgotten, by erasing it from hearts. ﴿We will bring a better one than it﴾, meaning: more suitable for those who are obligated to act by it, more beneficial for them, easier for them, and greater in its reward for them. ﴿Or its like﴾ in benefit and reward. ﴿Do you not know that Allah is over all things﴾ in respect of abrogation (naskh), substitution (tabdil) and other things, ﴿Competent﴾.

This verse was revealed when the polytheists said: "Muhammad orders his companions to do something, then forbids them from it, orders them to the opposite, says one thing today and retracts it tomorrow. This Qur'an is nothing but the words of Muhammad." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, and His saying: ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of another verse﴾ (Qur'an 16:101), and the rest of the verse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 107:

﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ He does in them what He wills, and He knows best the aspect of what is good in what He imposes upon them of abrogating (naskh) and abrogated (mansukh) [rulings]. ﴿And you have not, besides Allah, any protector or helper.﴾ That is: any walī (guardian, one who governs) who will take charge of your affairs and attend to them. ﴿Nor any helper﴾ who will give you victory. In this is a warning of His punishment, since there is nothing that can prevent it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 108:

﴿Am turidūn﴾ (Or do you wish?) means: Rather, do you wish ﴿that you ask your Messenger﴾, Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿as Moses was questioned before﴾? The reason for this is that the Quraysh said: "O Muhammad, make Safa into gold for us and widen the land of Makkah for us." So they were forbidden to propose signs to him, just as the people of Moses (peace be upon him) proposed when they said: ﴿Show us God plainly﴾. The reason is that asking after the proofs have been established is disbelief, and therefore He said: ﴿And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly strayed from the right way﴾, its middle and its direction.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 109:

﴿Many of the People of the Book wish⁠ ⁠⁠to turn you back, after you have believed, out of envy from their own selves⁠⁠﴾ This was revealed when the Jews said to the Muslims after the Battle of Uhud: "Did you not see what befell you? Had you been upon the truth, you would not have been defeated. So return to our religion." Thus is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Would that they could turn you back, after your belief, into disbelievers, out of envy from themselves⁠⁠﴾, i.e., in their judgments and their religious practice, that which they were not commanded to do, ﴿after the truth has become clear to them⁠⁠﴾ in the Torah, that the words of Muhammad (ﷺ) are true and his religion is right. ﴿So pardon and overlook⁠⁠﴾ and turn away from their bad characters, their speech, and the rancor of their hearts, ﴿until Allah brings His command⁠⁠﴾, i.e., the fighting.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 111:

﴿And they say: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews,﴾ That is: the Jews said, "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews," and the Christians said, "None will enter it except the Christians." ﴿These are their wishful beliefs.﴾ That is, the desires they wished for upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, falsely. ﴿Say: Produce your proof,﴾ that is, bring forward your argument for what you claim. Then he explained who will enter it, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 112:

﴿Yes﴾ — whoever ﴿submits his face to Allah﴾ (inqada li-amrihi, i.e., submits to His command and offers Him his face in prostration) ﴿while he is a doer of good﴾ (mu'min musaddiq bi-l-Qur'an, i.e., a believer who affirms the Qur'an).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 113:

﴿And the Jews say: "The Christians are not on anything."﴾ This was revealed when the delegation of Najran came, and they disputed with the Jews, and each of the two groups declared the other to be unbelievers.

And His saying, ﴿while they recite the Book﴾: meaning, both groups recite the Torah, and this disagreement has taken place between them, while their Book is one; by this He indicates their misguidance.

﴿Likewise said those who do not know﴾: meaning, the disbelievers of the earlier nations and the disbelievers of this ummah,

﴿the like of what they say﴾ in denying the prophets and opposing them. So the path of these people who recite the Book is like the path of those among the polytheists who do not know the Book, in rejecting the religion of Allah, glorified is He.

﴿So Allah will judge between them﴾: that is, He will show them with their own eyes who will enter Paradise and who will enter the Fire.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 114:**

﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah﴾. He means Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and those who fight against it. It was revealed concerning the people of Rome when they ruined Bayt al-Maqdis. ﴿Those﴾ means the people of Rome. ﴿It was not for them to enter them except in fear﴾. No Roman entered Bayt al-Maqdis, after the Muslims had built it, except in fear; if he were recognized, he would be killed. ﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾. He means killing for the *harbi* (the hostile non-Muslim combatant) and the *jizya* (the poll tax) for the *dhimmi* (the non-Muslim protected subject).

﴿And to Allah belong the east and the west﴾: that is, He is their Creator. It was revealed concerning some of the Companions who were travelling when a thick fog came upon them. They searched for the direction of the qibla and prayed facing different directions. When the fog lifted, it became clear that they had not faced it correctly. When they returned, they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about this.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾: that is, wherever you turn your faces. ﴿There is the Face of Allah﴾: that is, there is the qibla of Allah, the direction toward which Allah has commanded you to face in worship. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾: that is, Allah's law is vast, and He grants ease to His servants in their religion.

(The scholars differed over the ruling of this verse. Some of them said it has been abrogated (naskh) by His words, ﴿So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾. Others said its ruling remains in force, except that it applies specifically to voluntary prayers while travelling.)

It was also said that it was revealed concerning al-Najashi, when the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed over him together with his companions, and they said to him: "How do you pray over a man who prayed facing other than our qibla?" So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse and made clear that al-Najashi, even if he prayed toward the east or the west, intended thereby the Face of Allah and His worship.

The meaning of ﴿There is the Face of Allah﴾: that is, there is the good pleasure of Allah and His command, as in His words: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of Allah's Face﴾.

The words al-wajh (وجه, face), al-jihah (جهة, direction) and al-wijhah (وجهة, orientation) all mean: the qibla.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 116:

﴿And they say: "Allah has taken a son."﴾ That is, the Jews in their saying: ﴿"Uzayr is the son of Allah,"﴾ and the Christians in their saying: ﴿"The Messiah is the son of Allah,"﴾ and the polytheists in their saying: "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Then He exalted Himself above having a son, and said: ﴿Glory be to Him! Rather,﴾ the matter is not as they say. ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth,﴾ as slaves and as possessions. ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him,﴾ that is, obedient: meaning, those who obey Him, excluding not all of mankind.

Originator of the heavens and the earth (Badi'), their creator and bringer into being, not upon any prior pattern. ﴿And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ That is, He decrees it and wills its creation. ﴿He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ That is: He brings it into existence and it comes to be, and the condition is that His command relates to it. (The Ustadh Abu'l-Hasan said: He brings it into existence by His power, and it comes to be as He wills.)

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 118:

﴿And those who do not know said﴾: meaning the polytheists of the Arabs said to Muhammad (ﷺ): "We will not believe you until ﴿God speaks to us﴾ [that you are His Messenger], ﴿or a sign comes to us﴾." Meaning: [the signs] they asked for, namely the four signs in His Exalted saying: ﴿And they said: "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth"﴾ [Quran 17:90]. And the meaning of ﴿Why does God not speak to us?﴾ is: "Why does God not speak to us [and tell us] that you are His Messenger?" ﴿Thus said those before them﴾: meaning the disbelievers of the past nations, who disbelieved by being obstinate in demanding signs, just like these ones. ﴿Their hearts are alike﴾: some of them resembled one another in disbelief, harshness, and asking for the impossible. ﴿We have made the signs clear for a people who are certain﴾: meaning, whoever is certain and seeks the truth, the signs have come to him, because the Qur'an is a sufficient proof.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 119:

﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth﴾ — with the Qur'an and Islam. That is: with the truth, ﴿as a bringer of good tidings﴾, giving good news to the believers, ﴿and a warner﴾, frightening and cautioning the disbelievers. ﴿And you will not be asked about the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾. That is: you are not accountable for them. The reason for this is that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, were to send down His punishment upon the Jews, they would believe." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, meaning: there is no responsibility or liability upon you regarding their affairs.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 120:

﴿And the Jews will never be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their religion.﴾ The verse was revealed concerning the change of the qibla (direction of prayer). The Jews and the Christians had been hoping that Muhammad (ﷺ) would return to their religion. So when God, exalted is He, turned the qibla toward the Ka'ba, it weighed heavily on them, and they despaired of him ever agreeing with them in their religion. Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 121:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book﴾ — meaning: the believers among the Jews. ﴿Who recite it with its true recitation﴾ — they read it as it was revealed, do not distort it, and follow it with its true following.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 124:

﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord﴾ — i.e., He tried him, that is, dealt with him as one who tests ﴿with words﴾ — they are ten characteristics: five in the head, namely the parting of the hair (al-farq), rinsing the mouth (al-madmada), sniffing water into the nose (al-istinshaq), the siwak (tooth-cleaning stick), and trimming the moustache; and five in the body, namely: paring the nails, shaving the pubic area (al-'anah), circumcision (al-khitan), cleansing after relieving oneself (al-istinja'), and plucking the armpit hair (nataf al-raghghatayn). ﴿He fulfilled them﴾ — he performed them completely, without any shortfall. ﴿He said﴾ — God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people﴾ — the righteous will follow your example. Abraham said: ﴿And from my descendants?﴾ — i.e., also from my offspring, so appoint leaders who will be followed. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾ — He means: whoever among your offspring is a wrongdoer will not be a leader. And the meaning of ﴿My covenant﴾ — i.e., My prophethood.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 125:

﴿And [remember] when We made the House﴾, meaning the Ka'bah, ﴿a place of return (mathabah) for the people﴾, a destination (ma'ad) to which they return; they never tire of it, and whenever they depart they long for it again. ﴿And a sanctuary (amn)﴾, that is, a secure place (mu'minan). The Arabs would encounter a man who had killed his father within the sanctuary (haram) and would not molest him. As for today, the offender is not to be attacked if he seeks refuge in it, according to the people of Iraq. According to al-Shafi'i, it is preferable that he not be attacked, but if he is threatened by the enforcement of the prescribed punishment (hadd) upon him, it is permissible. Many of the exegetes have said: whoever wills, let him be secure, and whoever wills, let him not be secure, just as when He made it a place of return, whoever willed returned and whoever willed did not return. ﴿And take﴾, that is, the people, ﴿from the Station of Abraham (maqam Ibrahim)﴾, which is the stone known as the Station of Abraham, the place of his two feet, ﴿a place of prayer (musalla)﴾. This means that it is recommended to pray behind the Station. It has been recited in this form as a report (khabar), and it has also been recited with a kasrah as a command (amr). ﴿And We charged Abraham and Ishmael﴾, We commanded them and entrusted them, ﴿that purify My House﴾ from idols and impurities (al-rayb), ﴿for those who circumambulate (al-ta'ifin)﴾ around it, who are those who travel to it from the distant regions of the earth, ﴿and those who stay (al-'akifin)﴾, that is, those who remain in it, who are the inhabitants of the sanctuary, ﴿and those who bow (al-rukka')﴾, the plural of rakic, ﴿and prostrate (al-sujud)﴾, the plural of sajid, like qa'id and qu'ud.

﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this"﴾, that is, this place and this location, ﴿a city﴾, a dwelling, ﴿secure﴾, that is, possessing security, where its birds are not hunted, its trees are not cut down, and its people are not killed. ﴿And provide its people with fruits﴾, meaning the various kinds of produce of the trees, ﴿for those of them who believe in God and the Last Day﴾. Abraham (peace be upon him) specified the believers in the request for provision. God says: ﴿As for whoever disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little, then I will compel him﴾, that is, I will provide for him until the end of his term, ﴿then I will compel him﴾, that is, I will force him in the Hereafter ﴿to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination﴾. It.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 127:

﴿And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House, and Isma'il (with him), (they said):﴾ the foundations, the base of the structure, ﴿"Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."﴾ accept from us our drawing near to You by building this House; ﴿Indeed You are the All-Hearing﴾ of our supplication, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of what is in our hearts.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 128:

﴿Our Lord, and make us Muslims [submissive] to You﴾, obedient and submitting to Your command. ﴿And from our descendants, a community﴾, a group, ﴿Muslim [submissive] to You﴾, and they are the Muhajirun (Emigrants), the Ansar (Helpers), and those who follow them in goodness. ﴿And show us our rites﴾, make known to us our acts of worship.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 129:

﴿Our Lord, and raise up among them﴾ among the Muslim community, ﴿a messenger from among them﴾ he means Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and the wisdom﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿and purify them﴾ and cleanse them from shirk (association of partners with God), ﴿indeed You, You are the Exalted in Might﴾ the Victorious, the Powerful, whom nothing can overcome, and the explanation of "the Wise" has already passed.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 130:

﴿And who would turn away from the religion of Ibrahim﴾ i.e., none would turn away from it or abandon it, ﴿except one who makes a fool of himself﴾ i.e., who is ignorant of himself, not knowing that he is a creature of Allah the Exalted, who is obligated to worship his Creator. ﴿And We certainly chose him in this world﴾ i.e., We selected him for prophethood. ﴿And indeed, he is in the Hereafter among the righteous﴾ i.e., among the prophets.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 131:

﴿When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [Ibrahim was told:] devote your religion to Allah, glorified is He, in monotheism (tawhid). It is also said: surrender yourself to Allah. ﴿He said, "I have submitted"﴾ with my heart, my tongue and my limbs. ﴿To the Lord of the worlds.﴾

Wa-wassā bihā (And he enjoined it): that is, he commanded the religion (al-millah). It was also said: the word of sincere monotheism (kalimat al-ikhlas), Ibrahim enjoined upon his sons, and Ya'qub (did so): "O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you the religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims."

Ya bunayya (O my sons): he intended "an" ("that") here, meaning "that O my sons."

Inna Allaha stafa lakumu al-din (Indeed Allah has chosen for you the religion): that is, Islam, the religion of ḥanifiyyah (the upright, pure monotheistic faith).

Fa-la tamutunna illa wa-antum muslimun (So do not die except while you are Muslims): that is, hold fast to Islam, so that when death comes upon you, it finds you upon it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 133:

﴿Or were you witnesses﴾ He left the previous discussion and returned to addressing the Jews. The meaning: "Rather, were you witnesses," that is, present. ﴿When death approached Jacob﴾ This is because the Jews said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do you not know that when Jacob died he enjoined his sons to be Jews?" So God refuted them and said: "Were you present at his bequest ﴿when he said to his sons: "What will you worship after me?"﴾"

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 134:

﴿That is a nation﴾ meaning: Ibrahim and his sons, and Ya'qub and his sons, ﴿that has passed away﴾ meaning: has gone by. ﴿To it is what it earned﴾ from deeds. ﴿And to you﴾ O company of the Jews, ﴿is what you have earned﴾, meaning: their reckoning is upon them, and you will only be questioned about your own deeds.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 135:

﴿And they say: Be Jews or Christians, [you will be] guided.﴾ It was revealed concerning the Jews of Madinah and the Christians of Najran. Each of the two groups said to the believers: "Be upon our religion, for there is no religion except that." So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Rather, [we follow] the religion of Ibrahim, a ḥanīf.﴾ That is: "Rather, we follow the religion of Ibrahim, a ḥanīf, inclining away from all the religions to the religion of Islam." Then He commanded the believers that they should say:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 136:

﴿We believe in God and in what has been sent down to us﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. ﴿And in what was sent down to Ibrahim (Abraham), Isma'il (Ishmael), Ishaq (Isaac), Ya'qub (Jacob), and the tribes (al-asbat)﴾, who are the sons of Ya'qub. Among them were prophets, which is why He said: ﴿and what was sent down to them﴾. And His statement, exalted is He: ﴿We make no distinction between any of them﴾, i.e., we do not disbelieve in some and believe in others, as the Jews and the Christians did.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 137:

﴿If they believe in the like of what you believe in, then they have been guided.﴾ That is: if they bring a belief like your belief, and their faith is like your faith. ﴿Then they have been guided.﴾ That is, they have become Muslims. ﴿But if they turn away,﴾ that is, they turn away and refuse. ﴿Then they are only in opposition,﴾ that is, in dissension and enmity. ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them.﴾ Then He did so, and He sufficed him against the affair of the Jews: by killing and taking captives in Qurayzah, by expulsion and banishment in Banu al-Nadir, and by the jizya (poll tax) and humiliation among the Christians of Najran.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 138:

﴿Ṣibghat Allāh﴾ — that is: adhere to the religion of God. ﴿And who is better than God in ṣibgha?﴾ — that is: and who is better than God in religion?

Say, O Muhammad, to the Jews and the Christians: ﴿Do you dispute with us concerning God?﴾ (that is, do you argue with us about the religion of God?). This was because they said: "Our religion is the most ancient and our Book is the earliest, and if you were a prophet you would be one of us." ﴿And to us are our deeds﴾, we will be recompensed for their good and their evil, ﴿and you are [responsible] for your deeds, [following] the same path as ours﴾. ﴿And we are sincere to Him﴾, we are monotheists.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 140:

﴿Or do you say that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes were Jews or Christians?﴾ Say: ﴿Are you more knowing, or is God?﴾ That is: God, glorified is He, has informed us that the prophets' religion was Islam, and no one knows better than Him. ﴿And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from God?﴾ This is a rebuke to them: God, exalted is He, made them bear witness in the Torah and the Gospel that He would send among them Muhammad (ﷺ), from the descendants of Abraham, peace be upon him, and He took their covenant that they would make him clear and not conceal him. Then he mentioned the story of the change of the qibla, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 142:

﴿The foolish among the people will say﴾: meaning the polytheists of Makkah and the Jews of Madinah. ﴿What has turned them﴾: what has diverted them? They mean the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers ﴿from their qiblah which they had been facing﴾: and it was the rock. ﴿Say, to Allah belongs the east and the west﴾: He commands turning toward whichever direction He wills. ﴿He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾: a straight religion. He means: I have approved this qiblah for Muhammad (ﷺ). Then He praised his community, saying:

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 143:**

﴿وكذلك﴾ That is, just as We guided you to a straight path, ﴿جعلناكم أمة وسطاً﴾ *"We have made you a middle nation"*, meaning just, choice, and excellent, ﴿لتكونوا شهداء على الناس﴾ *"so that you may be witnesses over mankind"*, meaning that you bear witness against the nations that the prophets delivered the message, ﴿ويكون الرسول عليكم شهيداً﴾ *"and the Messenger may be a witness over you"*, meaning as to your truthfulness. This is because God, exalted is He, will question the nations on the Day of Resurrection, saying: "Did the messengers convey the message to you?" They will say: "No one has conveyed anything from You to us." Then the messengers will be questioned, and they will say: "We conveyed Your message to them, but they disobeyed." He will say: "Do you have a witness?" They will say: "Yes, the community of Muhammad (ﷺ)." So they will testify for them that they conveyed, and that their peoples denied them. The nations will say: "O Lord, how did they know that, when they came after us?" They will say: "Our Prophet informed us of that in his Book." Then Muhammad (ﷺ) will vouch for them.

﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا الْقِبْلَةَ الَّتِي كُنْتَ عَلَيْهَا﴾ *"And We did not make the qiblah that you used to face"*, meaning: the one you are facing today, which is the Ka'bah, a qiblah, ﴿إلاَّ لنعلم﴾ *"except that We might know"*, meaning: that We might see. It was also said that it means: that We might distinguish, ﴿مَنْ يتبع الرسول﴾ *"who follows the Messenger"*, in his affirmation of the abrogation (naskh) of the qiblah, ﴿ممن ينقلب على عقبيه﴾ *"from the one who turns back on his heels"*, meaning apostatizes and returns to disbelief. This is because God, exalted is He, made the abrogation of the qiblah from the Rock to the Ka'bah a trial for His believing servants. Whoever He protected affirmed the Messenger in that matter, and whoever He did not protect doubted his religion, his affair became confused for him, and he thought that Muhammad (ﷺ) was in confusion about his affair, so he apostatized from Islam. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً﴾ *"and it was indeed a great [matter]"*, that is: the turning toward the Ka'bah was indeed burdensome, ﴿إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ﴾ *"except for those whom God has guided"*, whom God protected through guidance. When the qiblah was changed, the Jews said: "What about the one among you who died while praying toward the first qiblah? He has died in misguidance." So God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إيمانكم﴾ *"And God would not let your faith be lost"*, that is: your prayers that you prayed and your affirmation of the first qiblah, ﴿إنَّ الله بالناس﴾ *"Indeed God is toward mankind"*, meaning: toward the believers, ﴿لرؤوف رحيم﴾ *"Kind and merciful"*. And ra'fah (kindness) is more intense than mercy (rahmah).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 144:

﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face﴾. The Ka'bah was the dearer of the two qiblahs (the direction of prayer) to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He saw that praying toward it would make his people more inclined to Islam, so he said to Jibril, peace be upon him: "I wish that Allah would turn me away from the qiblah of the Jews to another." Jibril, peace be upon him, said: "I am only a servant like you, and you are honored before your Lord, so ask Him." Then Jibril, peace be upon him, ascended, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kept gazing constantly at the sky, hoping that Jibril would bring him what he had asked for. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky﴾, that is, in looking toward the sky. ﴿So We will surely turn you to a qiblah that you will like﴾, that is, We will make you face a qiblah that you love and desire. ﴿So turn your face﴾, that is, direct your face ﴿toward the Sacred Mosque﴾, toward it and facing it. ﴿And wherever you are﴾, on land or at sea, and you intend to pray, ﴿turn your faces toward it﴾.

When the qiblah was changed to the Ka'bah, the Jews said: "O Muhammad, you were not commanded with this. It is only something you have innovated of your own accord." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth﴾, that the Sacred Mosque is the qiblah of Ibrahim and that it is true. ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾, O company of believers, of seeking My pleasure.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 145:

﴿And if you were to bring those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your qiblah.﴾ He means: the Jews and the Christians. ﴿Every sign﴾ (a proof and a miracle). ﴿They would not follow your qiblah﴾ because they are obstinate and deny your prophethood while knowing it.

﴿And you are not one who follows their qiblah﴾: by this he cut off the hopes of the Jews that the Prophet (ﷺ) would return to their qiblah, for they used to hope for that.

﴿And some of them are not followers of the qiblah of others﴾: he informed that they, although they are united in opposing the Prophet (ﷺ), disagree among themselves. So the Jews do not follow the qiblah of the Christians, and the Christians do not follow the qiblah of the Jews.

﴿And if you were to follow their desires﴾, that is, if you were to pray toward their qiblah ﴿after the knowledge that has come to you﴾ that the qiblah of God is the Ka'bah, ﴿then you would indeed be among the wrongdoers﴾. That is, you would then be just like them. The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ) outwardly, but in meaning it is to his community.

The commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on Surah 2, verse 146:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it (Muhammad ﷺ) as they recognize their own sons.﴾ They recognize Muhammad (ﷺ) by his description and attributes. ﴿And indeed a party of them conceal the truth﴾ concerning his description in the Torah, ﴿while they know.﴾ Because Allah has made that clear in their Book.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 147:

﴿The truth is from your Lord﴾ — i.e., this truth is from your Lord. ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾ — the ones who are in doubt regarding the matter that I have informed you of, concerning the qibla (direction of prayer) and the obstinacy of the Jews and their refusal to believe in you.

{Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 148:}

﴿And for each there is a direction⁠﻿ — i.e., for each people of a religion — a qiblah and a direction they face in prayer, ﴿toward which he turns his face⁠﻿ — i.e., facing it. ﴿So race to [all that is] good⁠﻿ — hasten to acceptance from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and turn your faces wherever Allah the Exalted has commanded you. ﴿Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you all together⁠﻿ — Allah the Exalted will gather you for reckoning, and then He will recompense you for your deeds.⁠﻿ Then he affirmed facing the qiblah wherever one is with two verses, and they are His, the Exalted's, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 150:

﴿And from wherever you set out﴾ — the verse, and His words: ﴿And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it, so that the people will have no argument against you﴾ — meaning: the Jews. The reason is that the Jews used to say: "Muhammad did not know where his qibla was until we guided him," and they would say: "Muhammad opposes us in our religion yet follows our qibla." This was their argument, with which they argued, deceiving the ignorant. When the qibla was turned to the Ka'bah, this argument was nullified. Then the Exalted said: ﴿except those of them who have done wrong﴾ — from among the people, and they are the polytheists, for they said: "Muhammad has turned to our qibla and knows that we are better guided in the way than he is." These are the ones who argue with falsehood. Then He said: ﴿So do not fear them﴾ — meaning: the polytheists, in their backing one another against you in disputation and fighting — ﴿but fear Me﴾ — in abandoning the qibla and opposing it. ﴿And that I may complete My favor upon you﴾ — i.e., and so that I may complete My favor upon you — the "that" is coordinated with ﴿so that﴾ — by My guiding you to the qibla of Abraham, so that the upright religion (al-millah al-hanifiyyah) is completed for you. ﴿And that you may be guided﴾ — and so that you may be guided to the qibla of Abraham.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 151:

﴿As We have sent among you﴾ The meaning: "And that I may complete My favour upon you, just as I sent to you a messenger," i.e., I complete this just as I completed that by sending to you. ﴿a messenger from among you﴾ whose truthfulness and lineage you know. ﴿reciting to you Our verses﴾ meaning: the Qur'an. This is an argument against them, because they knew that he was unlettered (ummi), who neither reads nor writes; so when he recited to them, his truthfulness in prophethood became clear to them. ﴿and purifying you﴾ i.e., he makes you reach that by which you become pure (azkiya'), through the command to obey Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 152:

﴿So remember Me﴾ through obedience, ﴿and I will remember you﴾ through forgiveness, ﴿and be grateful to Me﴾ for My blessings, ﴿and do not deny Me﴾, i.e., do not deny My blessings.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 153:

﴿O you who have believed, seek help﴾ in pursuing the Hereafter, ﴿through patience﴾ in carrying out the obligations, ﴿and prayer﴾, and through the five daily prayers for the expiation of sins. ﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾ That is: Indeed I am with you, I will support you and not forsake you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 154:

﴿And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive.﴾ It was revealed concerning the martyrs of Badr from among the Muslims. That is because they used to say, of whoever was killed in the way of Allah: "So-and-so has died, and the pleasures of this world have departed from him." So Allah the Exalted said: Do not say of those who were killed in My way, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, because the souls of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds that roam in Paradise, ﴿but you do not perceive﴾ what they are in of bliss and honour.

"And We will surely test you" — ﴿Wa-la-nabluwannakum﴾: meaning, "We will surely deal with you as one who tests," ﴿with something of fear﴾, meaning: fear of the enemy, ﴿and hunger﴾, meaning: famine, ﴿and a loss of wealth﴾, meaning: loss and diminution in property and the death of livestock, ﴿and lives﴾, meaning: death, killing in jihad, illness, and gray hair, ﴿and fruits﴾, meaning: calamities and the death of children. Whoever is patient with these things deserves the reward, and whoever is not patient does not deserve it. This is indicated by His saying, ﴿And give good tidings to the patient﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 156:

﴿Those who, when a misfortune strikes them﴾ of the kind mentioned, ﴿say: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we return."﴾ That is: our wealth belongs to Allah, and we are His servants; He does with us what He wills. Then He promised them forgiveness for this saying.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 157:

﴿Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord﴾, that is: forgiveness, ﴿and mercy﴾ and favour. ﴿And those are the rightly guided﴾ to Paradise, the reward, the truth and what is correct. It is said: [they are those who receive] an increase in guidance. It is said: they are those who benefit from being guided.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 158:

﴿Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah﴾ — two known mountains in Makkah — ﴿are among the symbols of Allah﴾, that is, among the places of His worship. ﴿So whoever performs Hajj to the House﴾ visits it, magnifying it, ﴿or performs ʿUmrah﴾ intends the House for visitation, ﴿there is no sin upon him﴾, meaning there is no wrongdoing upon him, ﴿for going back and forth between them﴾, between the two mountains. This is because the people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period of ignorance) used to circle between them while there were two idols upon them, which they would rub. So the Muslims disliked circling between them, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. ﴿And whoever volunteers good﴾ does what is not obligatory upon him, of circumambulation, prayer, zakat, and obedience, ﴿then indeed Allah is Appreciative﴾, rewarding him for his deed, ﴿Knowing﴾ of his intention.

ſ﴿Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down﴾ — meaning: the scholars of the Jews — ﴿of the clear proofs﴾ — concerning stoning, the prescribed punishments, and the rulings — ﴿and the guidance﴾ — the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his description — ﴿after We have made it clear to the people﴾ — to the Children of Israel — ﴿in the Book﴾ — in the Torah — ﴿those, Allah curses them, and those who curse invoke a curse upon them﴾ — everything except the jinn and mankind.

Qur'anic quotations are in ﴿ ﴾ markers. Translating:

﴿Except those who repent﴾ return from concealment, ﴿and amend﴾ their inner state, ﴿and make clear﴾ the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿then those, I will turn back to them in mercy﴾, I will return to them with forgiveness.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 161:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of mankind, all together.﴾ Meaning: the believers.

Abiding therein forever: the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be given respite. That is: nor will they be granted a delay for return (to the world), repentance, or an excuse, since the obligation (to act) has already ceased.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 163:

﴿And your God is one God﴾. The idolaters had three hundred and sixty idols that they worshipped besides Allah, may He be glorified and exalted. So Allah, glorified is He, made clear that He is their God and that He is one. He said: ﴿And your God is one God﴾, meaning: He has no partner in divinity, and there is none like Him in His essence, ﴿there is no god but Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate﴾. Allah, mighty and majestic, refuted them for associating other gods with Him. The idolaters marvelled at this and said: "Muhammad says: ﴿And your God is one God﴾. Let him then bring us a sign, if he is among the truthful." So Allah, exalted, sent down:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 164:

﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ with their greatness and the multitude of their parts, ﴿and the alternation of the night and the day﴾ their going and their coming, ﴿and the ship﴾ the ships ﴿which run in the sea with that which benefits people﴾ of trade, ﴿and what Allah sends down from the sky of water﴾ of rain, ﴿and gives life thereby to the earth﴾ makes it fertile after its barrenness, ﴿and scatters﴾ spreads ﴿therein creatures of every kind﴾, ﴿and the turning of the winds﴾ their being turned, sometimes from the south and sometimes from the north, and cold and hot, ﴿and the clouds subjected﴾ made subservient to the command of Allah ﴿between the sky and the earth﴾ ﴿are signs﴾ indications of the oneness of Allah ﴿for a people who use their intellect﴾. So Allah, mighty and majestic, taught them through this verse the manner of reasoning to the Creator and to His oneness, and directed them to reflect upon His signs and to consider His creation. Then He informed that a people, after these signs and clear proofs, take rivals (to Allah), though they know that they bring none of what has been mentioned; so He said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 165:

﴿And among the people are those who take, besides Allah, equals (andad)﴾. He means: the idols, which are equals (andad), some of them to others, i.e., likenesses. ﴿They love them as they love Allah﴾, i.e., as the believers love Allah. ﴿But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah﴾, because the disbeliever turns away from his object of worship in the time of trial, whereas the believer does not turn away from Allah in ease and hardship, in prosperity and adversity. ﴿If only those who did wrong﴾, i.e., disbelieved, ﴿could see when they see the punishment﴾, the severity of Allah's punishment and His might, ﴿they would know that the harm lies in taking equals (andad)﴾. The answer to (law, "if only") is omitted, and it is what we have mentioned.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 166:

﴿When those who were followed disowned those who followed them﴾. This verse is connected to what precedes it, because the meaning is: Allah is severe in punishment when those who were followed in polytheism disown their followers upon seeing the punishment, saying: "We did not call you to misguidance and to what you were" ﴿and their ties were cut off from them﴾, the connections that existed between them in the world, of kinship and affection, and their friendship turned into enmity.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 167:

﴿And those who followed will say﴾: they are the followers (al-atba'). ﴿If only we had a return (karrah) to the world and a chance to go back, we would disown them﴾ ﴿as they have disowned us.﴾ ﴿Thus﴾ means: as some of them disown others. ﴿Allah will show them their deeds as regrets upon them﴾: meaning, their worship of idols, hoping that it would bring them near to Allah the Exalted. So when they were punished for what they had hoped for in its reward, they were overcome with regret.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 168:

﴿O mankind, eat of what is on earth [that is] lawful and good﴾ This verse was revealed concerning those who forbade for themselves the sawa'ib (freed camels), the wasa'il (sheep that bore twins), and the bahira (she-camels whose ears were slit). So God, glory be to Him, informed them that eating these is lawful, and that their prohibition is from the work of Satan. Then He said: ﴿And do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾, i.e., his ways and paths. Then He clarified Satan's enmity, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 169:

﴿Indeed, he commands you only to evil﴾ [i.e., to acts of disobedience (ma'asi)] ﴿and immorality﴾ [i.e., stinginess (bukhl)]. It was also said: [it refers to] every sin for which there is a prescribed punishment (hadd). ﴿And that you say about Allah what you do not know﴾ [i.e., concerning the prohibition of the cattle and the tilth].

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 170:

﴿And when it is said to them﴾ i.e., to those who had forbidden certain things from the tilth and the cattle: ﴿"Follow what Allah has sent down,"﴾ they say: ﴿"No, we will follow what we found our fathers upon."﴾ Then Allah, the Exalted, rebuking them, says: ﴿"Even though their fathers understood nothing and were not guided?"﴾ Will they follow them? The meaning is: Will they follow their fathers even if they were ignorant?! Then He struck a parable for the disbelievers, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 171:

﴿And the likeness of those who disbelieve﴾ in their admonition and their calling to God, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿is like the one who shouts to that which hears nothing but a call and a cry﴾ — the shepherd ﴿who shouts﴾ (yan'iq), i.e., cries out, to the sheep, which ﴿do not understand anything﴾. The meaning of yan'iq is: he cries out. He means: the beasts that do not understand and do not comprehend what the shepherd says; they only hear a sound whose meaning they do not know. Likewise, those who disbelieve hear the words of the Prophet (ﷺ), but they are like sheep, since they do not act upon what he commanded them. The explanation of His saying ﴿deaf, dumb, blind﴾ has already passed. Then he mentioned that what the polytheists forbade is lawful, so he said:

O you who have believed, eat of the good things that We have provided for you. That is: the lawful (ḥalālāt) of what We have provided for you of the crops and the livestock, and of what the polytheists made unlawful for themselves of these two. ﴿And be grateful to Allah, if it is Him that you worship.﴾ That is: if worship of Allah is obligatory upon you, since He is your God, then thanking Him is obligatory, since He is the One who bestows favour upon you. Then he explained what is forbidden, what it is, and said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 173:

﴿Indeed, He has forbidden to you only carrion﴾, which is everything from which the soul has departed without proper slaughter (dhakah) among what is slaughtered, ﴿and blood﴾, meaning flowing blood, due to His saying in another place: ﴿or blood poured forth﴾. Both of these categories have been qualified (takhsis) by the Sunnah, namely [his saying ﷺ: "Two carcasses and two bloods have been made lawful for us"]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and the flesh of swine﴾, meaning swine in all its parts; flesh was singled out because it is the thing intended for eating. ﴿And that which has been dedicated to other than Allah﴾, meaning what was slaughtered for idols, so that other than the name of Allah was invoked over it. ﴿But whoever is compelled﴾, i.e., is driven and forced by necessity (darurah). It is also said: whoever is coerced into consuming it and compelled to eat it, just as one is compelled to utter falsehood. ﴿Neither desiring [it] nor transgressing﴾, i.e., not an armed robber who cuts off the road, not one who separates from the rulers (al-a'immah) or opposes the community (al-ummah). ﴿Nor exceeding [the need]﴾, nor a wrongdoer who oversteps, and [then] eats; ﴿there is no sin upon him﴾. This indicates that one who is sinful in his journey is not permitted to eat carrion in cases of necessity. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ of disobedience, so He does not hold to account for that in which He has granted the concession; ﴿Merciful﴾, in that He has granted concession to the one under necessity.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 174:

﴿Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has revealed of the Book﴾ — he means: the leaders of the Jews. ﴿And exchange it for a small price﴾ — with what Allah revealed concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) in their book. ﴿A small price﴾ — he means: what they take in bribes (rushaa, sing. rishwa, "bribe") for concealing his description. ﴿Those — they consume not into their bellies except the Fire﴾ — except that whose ultimate end is the Fire. ﴿And Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ — that is, speech that would gladden them. ﴿Nor will He purify them﴾ — nor will He cleanse them from the defilement of their sins.

﴿Those are the ones who have bought misguidance﴾ in exchange for ﴿guidance, and punishment⁠⁠ in exchange for forgiveness﴾, when they denied the command of Muhammad (ﷺ) and concealed his description. ﴿How patient they are in the Fire!﴾ That is: what made them endure the Fire and what called them to it, when they abandoned the truth and followed falsehood?! This is a question whose meaning is rebuke for them. (It was also said: "How bold they are toward the Fire!")

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 176:

﴿That﴾, i.e., that punishment is theirs, ﴿because God has sent down the Book with the truth﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿yet they differed concerning it﴾. ﴿And indeed those who differed concerning the Book﴾ said that it is rajaz (a type of verse with a fixed rhythmic meter), poetry, soothsaying, and sorcery, ﴿are in far-reaching dissension﴾, meaning in long-standing opposition to the truth.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 177:

﴿It is not righteousness﴾ At the beginning of Islam, a man who bore witness to the two testimonies (shahadatayn) and prayed toward whichever direction it was, and then died in that state, was assured of Paradise. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) migrated, the obligatory duties were revealed, and the qibla was turned toward the Ka'bah, Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, saying: ﴿It is not righteousness﴾ in its entirety ﴿that you turn your faces toward the east or the west﴾ and do not do anything other than that. ﴿But righteousness﴾ means: the one who possesses righteousness is ﴿he who believes in Allah and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets, and gives wealth, despite love for it﴾, i.e., despite love for wealth (and it was said: the pronoun refers to giving). ﴿To relatives﴾ It was said: this refers to the relatives of the Prophet (ﷺ) (and it was said: it means the relatives of the deceased). ﴿And the wayfarer﴾ is the one cut off from his means who passes by you, and the guest who comes down upon you. ﴿And for freeing slaves﴾ i.e., for their price, meaning: those who are seeking manumission (mukatabun). ﴿And those who fulfill their promise when they promise﴾ to Allah or to people. ﴿And the patient in poverty﴾ (al-ba's: poverty) ﴿and adversity﴾ (al-darra': illness) ﴿and at the time of battle﴾ (hin al-ba's: the time of fighting in the way of Allah). ﴿Those are﴾ the people of this description ﴿who are the truthful﴾ in their faith.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 178:

﴿O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution (al-qisas) for those murdered﴾ It was revealed concerning two tribes of the Arabs, one of which was more noble than the other. The lesser of them killed some people from the nobler one, so the nobler said: "We will certainly kill the free man for the slave, and the male for the female, and we will certainly multiply the wounds," so God the Exalted revealed this verse. His words ﴿prescribed﴾ (kutiba): obligated and made obligatory. ﴿For you, legal retribution﴾ (al-qisas): observing equivalence and parity between the slain, so that it is not permissible for a free man to be killed for a slave, or a Muslim for a disbeliever. Observing equivalence is therefore obligatory, and this is His words: ﴿the free for the free, and the slave for the slave, and the female for the female﴾. His words in Surat al-Ma'idah, ﴿that the soul is for the soul﴾, indicate that the male is killed for the female, so a free man is killed for a free woman. ﴿But whoever is pardoned﴾, i.e., has something left to him of the blood ﴿of his brother﴾, the one slain, ﴿something﴾, namely that some of the guardians pardon and the retaliation is dropped. ﴿Then pursuit should be made in a reasonable manner﴾, i.e., the pardoning guardian, who is the guardian of the blood, should pursue the killer in a reasonable manner, which is to demand the wealth from him without harshness and harm, and upon the one from whom the wealth is demanded is ﴿payment﴾, the rendering of the wealth to the one who pardoned, ﴿with good conduct﴾, which is to avoid procrastination and delay. ﴿That is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy﴾: that God the Exalted gave this community the choice between retaliation, blood-money (diyah), and pardon, and this was granted only to this community. ﴿But whoever transgresses﴾, i.e., wrongs by killing the killer after taking the blood-money, ﴿for him is a painful punishment﴾.

﴿And for you in retaliation there is life﴾, meaning: in its establishment there is life. For when a killer is put to death, everyone who intends to kill is deterred from killing, so retaliation becomes a cause of life for the one who would be killed and also for the would-be killer, for if he kills, he will be killed. ﴿O you who possess intellect﴾, O you who have reason, ﴿that you may be mindful of God﴾, [avoiding] the shedding of blood out of fear of retaliation.

﴿It is prescribed for you﴾. The people of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance) used to bequeath their wealth to distant people out of showing off and seeking fame, and they left their poor relatives destitute. So God the Exalted revealed this verse. ﴿It is prescribed for you﴾: it was made obligatory and required for you. ﴿When death approaches any of you﴾: that is, its signs and precursors. ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾: money. ﴿A bequest to parents and relatives in a fair manner﴾: that is, it should not exceed one-third. ﴿A duty﴾: that is, this is a right, a rightful duty. ﴿Upon the God-conscious﴾: those who guard themselves against polytheism (shirk). This verse has been abrogated (naskh) by the verse of inheritance, and a bequest is not obligatory upon anyone. (And a bequest to an heir is not permissible.)

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 181:

﴿Then whoever alters it after he has heard it﴾, i.e., whoever alters the bequest, changing it, whether he is the executor, the guardian, or the witness, after he has heard it from the deceased, ﴿then its sin is only upon those who alter it﴾, the sin of the alteration, ﴿and the deceased is absolved﴾. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing﴾, hearing what the testator said, ﴿Knowing﴾ of his intention and what he meant. The guardians and executors used to carry out the deceased's bequest after the revelation of this verse, even if it consumed the whole estate, until Allah the Exalted revealed:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 182:

﴿Then whoever fears﴾ that is: knows ﴿from a testator (mooṣin) injustice (janafan)﴾ meaning error in the bequest, without intention, namely that he bequeaths to some of his heirs, or bequeaths all of his wealth, by mistake ﴿or sin (ithman)﴾ that is: deliberately, by intentional inclination; so he fears from the bequest and does what is not permitted, knowingly ﴿then makes peace (fa-aṣlaḥa)﴾ after his death between his heirs and those to whom the bequest was made ﴿then there is no sin upon him﴾ that is: he is not one who alters (the bequest) and thereby incurs sin; rather he is an intermediary for reconciliation, and there is no sin upon him.

ﷻ "O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you that you may become righteous."

Here "fasting" (ṣiyām) means the fasting of the month of Ramadan. "As it was prescribed" means "as it was made obligatory." "Those before you" means: you are commanded to worship through fasting just as those before you were commanded to worship. "That you may become righteous" means: so that you may refrain from eating, drinking and sexual intercourse during the time when fasting is obligatory.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 184:

﴿Days numbered.﴾ That is, the month of Ramadan. ﴿So whoever among you is sick or on a journey﴾ and breaks the fast, ﴿then a number [of fasts]﴾ — that is, then upon him is a number, meaning the fasting of a number equal to what he broke, ﴿from other days﴾ besides the days of his illness and his journey. ﴿And for those who are able to fast, there is a ransom: the feeding of a poor person.﴾ This was at the beginning of Islam: whoever was able to fast was permitted to break the fast and feed a poor person, one mudd of food, for each day. It was abrogated (naskh) by His saying: ﴿So whoever of you witnesses the month, let him fast it.﴾ ﴿And whoever volunteers good, it is better for him.﴾ He increased the ransom beyond one mudd. ﴿And that you fast is better for you.﴾ That is, fasting is better for you than breaking the fast and paying the ransom. And this [ruling] was before the abrogation.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 185:

﴿Shahru Ramadan﴾ (the month of Ramadan): meaning, those counted days are the month of Ramadan. ﴿In which the Qur'an was sent down﴾: it was sent down all at once from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) on the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) in the month of Ramadan, and was placed in the House of Honour (Bayt al-'Izzah) in the lowest heaven. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) brought it down upon Muhammad (ﷺ) in installments, piece by piece, over twenty years. ﴿A guidance for the people﴾: guiding the people. ﴿And clear proofs of guidance﴾: clear verses concerning the lawful and the unlawful, the prescribed limits and the rulings. ﴿And the Criterion﴾: the distinction between truth and falsehood. ﴿So whoever of you witnesses the month﴾: whoever of you is present in his town during the month ﴿let him fast it﴾. ﴿And whoever is ill or on a journey, then a number of other days﴾: he repeated here the option for the sick and the traveller, because the first verse came with the option for the sick, the traveller and the resident, and in this verse the option for the resident was abrogated (nuskh), so the mention of the option for the sick and the traveller was repeated so that it would be known that it remains as it was. ﴿Allah intends ease for you﴾: through the concession for the traveller and the sick. ﴿And He does not intend hardship for you﴾: because He did not make it strict or constrict you. ﴿And that you complete the period﴾ (conjoined to an omitted clause); the meaning is: Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship for you, so that it may be easy for you. ﴿And that you complete the period﴾: meaning, that you complete the number of days you broke fasting by making them up (qada') when you are resident and recovered. ﴿And that you glorify Allah﴾: meaning the takbir on the night of Eid al-Fitr when the crescent of Shawwal is sighted. ﴿For what He has guided you to﴾: He has directed you in the laws of the religion.

"And when My servants ask you about Me, [say:] indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me..." — ﴿And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near; I respond to the call of the caller when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me that they may be guided.﴾

Some of the Companions asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "Is our Lord near, so that we may confide in Him privately, or is He far, so that we must call out to Him?" So God the Exalted revealed this verse. His saying, ﴿Indeed I am near﴾, means: His nearness is by His knowledge. ﴿I respond﴾ means: I hear ﴿the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me﴾. ﴿So let them respond to Me﴾ means: let them answer Me with obedience and by affirming the messengers, ﴿and believe in Me, that they may be guided﴾, so that they may be hopeful of attaining right guidance.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 187:

﴿Permitted for you on the night of the fast﴾ the verse. At the beginning of Islam, intercourse was not permitted on the nights of fasting, nor eating or drinking after the night prayer (ʿishāʾ). So Allah the Exalted permitted all of that until the break of dawn. As for His saying: ﴿Going in unto your wives (al-rafath)﴾, meaning: the going in to them (al-ifḍāʾ) by intercourse. ﴿They are a garment (libās) for you﴾, i.e., a bedding (firāsh). ﴿And you are a garment for them﴾, a covering (liḥāf) ﴿for them﴾ during intercourse. ﴿Allah knew that you were deceiving yourselves﴾, you were betraying yourselves by intercourse during the nights of Ramadan. This was because ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, and others did that, then they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asking him, so the concession was revealed. ﴿So He turned to you (in forgiveness)﴾, meaning He returned to you with the concession. ﴿And pardoned you﴾ for what you had done before the concession. ﴿So now, have relations with them (bāshirūhunna)﴾, meaning have intercourse with them, ﴿and seek﴾, and seek out, ﴿what Allah has decreed for you﴾, meaning what Allah the Glorified has ordained for you of offspring. ﴿And eat and drink﴾ throughout the night ﴿until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread﴾, meaning: the whiteness of the dawn ﴿from the black thread﴾, the blackness of the night, ﴿from the dawn﴾, an explanation that this white thread is from the dawn and not from anything else. ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾ by abstaining from these things. ﴿And do not have relations with them while you are staying in the mosques for worship (ʿākifūn)﴾, a prohibition on the one in seclusion (muʿtakif) from intercourse, because it invalidates it. ﴿These﴾, i.e., these rulings which were mentioned, ﴿are the limits of Allah﴾, His prohibitions. ﴿So do not approach them﴾, do not commit them. ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., like this clarification, ﴿Allah makes clear His verses to the people that they may become righteous﴾ by avoiding what is forbidden.

"Do not consume one another's wealth by false means" — that is, let none of you consume another's property by what is not lawful in the Sharia, such as betrayal, usurpation, theft, gambling, and other such things. ﴿and proffer it to the authorities﴾ — and do not bribe the rulers with your wealth (i.e., do not offer bribes) so that you might seize the right of others. ﴿so that you may consume a portion﴾ — a group — ﴿of people's wealth through sin﴾ — by bribing the ruler so that he judges in your favour — ﴿while you know﴾ that you are wrongdoers and that it is not lawful for you. The original meaning of *al-idla'* (proffering) is sending forth, from their saying: "adlaytu al-dalw" (I lowered the bucket).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 189:

﴿They ask you about the new moons.﴾ Mu'adh ibn Jabal asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the waxing and waning of the moon, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿They ask you about the new moons.﴾ The word "ahilla" (new moons) is the plural of "hilal" (the crescent). ﴿Say: They are times marked out for people and for the Hajj.﴾ Allah informed that the wisdom in its waxing and waning is the removal of confusion from people's times: in their pilgrimage, the due dates of their debts, the waiting periods of their women, the wages of their hired workers, the terms of their pregnant animals and women, and other such matters.

﴿It is not righteousness to enter houses from their backs.﴾ When a man in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) entered the state of ihram, he would breach the back of his house with an opening through which he would enter and exit. So Allah commanded them to abandon the custom of the Jahiliyyah and informed them that this is not righteousness. ﴿But righteousness is [in] one who fears [Allah].﴾ Righteousness is the one who avoids opposing Allah. ﴿And enter houses through their doors.﴾ The verse.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 190:**

﴿And fight in the way of Allah﴾ [to the end of the verse]. This verse was revealed concerning the treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned back from al-Hudaybiyyah to al-Madinah al-Munawwarah, after the polytheists had prevented him from reaching the House, he made a treaty with them that he would return the following year and that they would vacate Makkah for him for three days. When the following year came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions prepared for ʿUmrat al-Qadaʾ (the make-up ʿumrah). They feared that Quraysh would not keep its word to them, that they would bar them from the House, and that they would fight them. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked fighting them in the sacred month and within the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram).
