So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And fight in the way of Allah﴾, that is, in the religion of Allah and in obedience to Him, ﴿those who fight you﴾, meaning Quraysh, ﴿but do not transgress﴾, that is, do not wrong them by beginning the fighting within the Sacred Precinct.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 191:

﴿And kill them wherever you find them﴾ — that is, wherever you come upon them and capture them. ﴿And expel them from where they expelled you﴾ — meaning: from Makkah. ﴿And fitnah is worse than killing﴾ — meaning: their associating partners with Allah, the Exalted, is greater than your killing them in the sacred precinct. ﴿And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you therein﴾ — they were forbidden to initiate killing or fighting until the polytheists begin. ﴿But if they fight you, then kill them﴾ — that is, if they initiate fighting with you at al-Masjid al-Haram, then you have the right to fight them by way of retaliation. Then he explained that if they desist — that is, cease from shirk, disbelief and fighting, and embrace Islam — ﴿then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ — that is, He will forgive them their earlier disbelief and fighting, and He bestows favour upon them by accepting their repentance and their faith after their disbelief and fighting.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 193:

﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾, that is, shirk (associating partners with God). Meaning: fight them until they submit to Islam, and a jizyah (poll tax) is not accepted from a pagan polytheist. ﴿And religion is for Allah﴾, that is, obedience and worship are for Allah ﴿alone﴾, so nothing is worshipped besides Him. ﴿But if they desist﴾ from disbelief, ﴿then there is no aggression﴾, that is, no killing and no plundering, ﴿except against the wrongdoers﴾ and the disbelievers.

﴿The sacred month for the sacred month﴾. That is: if they fight you in the sacred month, then fight them in its like. ﴿And the sacred things are subject to retaliation﴾. That is: if they violate a sanctity of yours, then violate theirs in the same way. Allah, glorified is He, informed that it is not permitted for the Muslims to violate them by way of initiating, but only by way of retaliation (qisas), and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾, the verse.

"And spend in the way of Allah"—in obedience to Allah the Exalted, through jihad and other than it—"and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction"—and do not withhold from spending in jihad—"and do good"—that is, [think well of] Allah the Exalted regarding the reward and the replacement He will give you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 196:

﴿And complete the Hajj and the ʿUmrah for Allah﴾ — with their rites (manasik), their limits (hudud), their sunan, and the performance of everything in them. ﴿But if you are prevented﴾ — held back and barred from completing them. ﴿Then what is easy﴾ — then it is obligatory upon you to give what is feasible ﴿of the sacrificial offering (hady)﴾ — which is what is brought as an offering to the House of Allah, the Exalted. The best of it is a camel (badanah), the middle of it is a cow, and the least of it is a sheep. So upon him is what is feasible from these kinds. ﴿And do not shave your heads﴾ — meaning, do not exit your state of ihram ﴿until the offering reaches its place of sacrifice (mahill)﴾ — until the offering is slaughtered in Makkah according to some opinions, and this is the position of the people of Iraq. In another opinion, its place of sacrifice is wherever its slaughter and sacrifice are permitted, which is where one is prevented; this is the position of al-Shafiʿi. ﴿So whoever among you is ill or has an injury to his head﴾ — meaning, vermin falling into the hair and multiplying, so he shaves ﴿then a ransom of fasting﴾ — which is fasting three days ﴿or giving charity﴾ — which is feeding six needy persons, two mudd for each needy person ﴿or a sacrifice﴾ — a slaughtered animal. ﴿When you are secure﴾ — meaning, from the enemy, or when the pilgrimage is one in which there is no fear of an enemy ﴿then whoever performs tamattuʿ (enjoyment) by ʿumrah to Hajj﴾ — meaning, he arrives in Makkah in the state of ihram, performs ʿumrah during the months of Hajj, remains in a state of non-ihram in Makkah until he begins the Hajj from it in that same year, and enjoys what is forbidden in ihram because he has been released by the ʿumrah. Whoever does this, ﴿then﴾ upon him ﴿is what is feasible of the sacrificial offering. But whoever does not find﴾ the price of the offering ﴿then fasting three days during﴾ the months of ﴿the Hajj and seven when you return﴾ — meaning, after finishing the Hajj ﴿These are ten complete﴾ — ﴿that﴾ meaning, that obligation which we were commanded, of the offering or the fasting ﴿is for those whose families are not present at al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ — meaning, for those who are not people of Makkah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 197:

﴿The Hajj is in well-known months.﴾ That is: the months of the Hajj are well-known months, ﴿known and specified, fixed in time﴾, and they are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and nine days of Dhu al-Hijjah. ﴿So whoever undertakes the Hajj therein﴾ makes it obligatory upon himself through the ihram and the talbiyah. ﴿Then there is no sexual relations (rafath)﴾, meaning no intercourse, ﴿nor wickedness (fusuq)﴾, meaning no acts of disobedience, ﴿nor disputing﴾, which is to argue with one's companion until one angers him. The meaning is: do not commit rafath, do not commit fusuq, and do not dispute ﴿during the Hajj. And whatever good you do, Allah knows it﴾, that is: Allah, the All-Knowing, will reward you for it. ﴿And take provision﴾. It was revealed concerning a people who used to perform the Hajj without provisions, saying: "We rely upon Allah (mutawakkilun)." Then they would ask people for help, and sometimes they would wrong and seize from them. So Allah commanded them to take provision, saying ﴿And take provision﴾, that by which you sustain yourselves. ﴿Indeed, the best provision is taqwa (God-consciousness)﴾, meaning: that by which you restrain your faces from asking and your selves from wrongdoing.

﴿And there is no blame upon you﴾. Some people used to claim that there was no hajj (pilgrimage) for a merchant or a camel driver. So God, exalted is He, informed them that there is no sin in seeking provision through His words: ﴿There is no blame upon you in seeking bounty from your Lord﴾, that is, provision through trade during the hajj. ﴿Then when you pour forth﴾, that is, when you depart and leave ﴿from ʿArafat, remember God﴾ with supplication and the talbiyah (the pilgrim's call of "Labbayk"), ﴿at the sacred landmark (al-Mashʿar al-Ḥaram)﴾. ﴿And remember Him as He has guided you﴾, that is, a remembrance like His guidance to you, meaning that it is to be a recompense for His guiding you. ﴿And indeed, before that, you were among the astray﴾, that is, before His guidance you were only misguided.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 199:

﴿Then depart from where the people depart.﴾ He means: the Arabs and the common people, except the Quraysh. That is because they used not to stand at ʿArafat but would stand at al-Muzdalifah, saying, "We are the people of the Sacred Precinct of God, so we do not leave it." So God commanded them to stand at ʿArafat as the rest of the people do, so that the departure (al-ifadah) would be with them from there. ﴿Then when you have completed your rites (manasik)﴾ that is: when you have finished your acts of worship which you were commanded to perform in the Hajj. ﴿Then remember God as you remember your fathers﴾ The Arabs, when they had finished their Hajj, would recount the glorious deeds of their forefathers, so God, mighty and majestic, commanded them to remember Him instead. ﴿Or with a greater remembrance﴾ meaning: and with a greater remembrance. ﴿Among the people are those who say, "Our Lord, give us in this world"﴾ and they are the polytheists, who used to ask for wealth, camels and sheep, and did not ask for any share in the Hereafter, because they did not believe in it. The Muslims ask for a share in both this world and the Hereafter, and that is His saying:

ـ﴿And among them is one who says: "Our Lord, give us in this world good, and in the Hereafter good, and save us from the punishment of the Fire."﴾ Verse 201 of Surah al-Baqarah is cited here in the commentary's own quotation, so I render it fully only where it appears in the source. Translating the text as given:

﴿And among them is one who says, "Our Lord, give us in the world good"﴾. The meaning of "good in the world" (ḥasanah fī al-dunyā) is: acting in a way that pleases Allah. And "good in the Hereafter" (ḥasanah fī al-ākhirah) is: Paradise.

Translation:

﴿Those will have a share of what they have earned.﴾ That is: the reward for what they did. ﴿And Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ With these people, because He forgives their misdeeds and multiplies their good deeds.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 203:

﴿And remember Allah during the appointed days.﴾ It means: the takbir (glorification of Allah, saying "Allahu akbar") after the prayers during the days of tashriq (the days of drying meat, the 11th, 12th and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah).

﴿Whoever hastens in two days﴾ of the days of tashriq, and departs on the second day from Mina, ﴿there is no sin upon him﴾ for his hastening.

﴿And whoever delays﴾ from departing until the third day, ﴿there is no sin upon him﴾ for his delay.

﴿For those who fear Allah.﴾ That is: the removal of sin is for those who, in their hajj, are mindful of not neglecting anything that Allah the Exalted has set as a limit.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 204:

﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the life of this world pleases you⁠—﴾ meaning: al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, who was a hypocrite, sweet of speech, pleasing in outward appearance, and evil in inward disposition. And [the phrase] ﴿about the life of this world﴾ [means] because his speech only pleases people in this world, and he has no reward for it in the Hereafter. ﴿And he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾ because he used to say to the Prophet (ﷺ): "By Allah, I truly believe in you and love you." ﴿Yet he is the most stubborn of opponents﴾ meaning: most vehement in dispute, and he was a disputer in falsehood.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 205:

﴿And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein, and destroys the crops and the animals﴾ (the verse). The reason for its revelation is that he returned to Makkah, passed by a field of crops and donkeys belonging to the Muslims, set fire to the crops and hamstrung the donkeys. This is what is meant by His words: ﴿and destroys the crops and the animals﴾, i.e., the offspring of the beasts.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 206:

﴿When it is said to him, "Fear Allah"﴾ And when it is said to him: "Gently, gently!" ﴿pride seizes him to sin﴾ The arrogance and the zealotry of the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) move him to act sinfully. ﴿Hell is sufficient for him﴾ Hellfire suffices him as his recompense. ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾ And wretched is the place of rest, Hell.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 207:

﴿And among the people is one who sells himself﴾ that is, sells (yabi') himself, meaning: he gives himself up to the commands of God, Exalted is He, ﴿seeking the pleasure of God﴾, to seek the approval of God. It was revealed concerning Suhayb al-Rumi.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 208:

﴿O you who have believed, enter into peace (al-silm) completely (kaffah)﴾ meaning: into Islam, ﴿completely﴾ meaning: all of it, i.e., in all of its legislations. It was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions, because after they had entered Islam, they venerated the Sabbath and disliked the flesh of camels, so they were commanded to abandon that, and that the prohibition of the Sabbath and the disliking of camel meat are not among the legislations of Islam. ﴿And do not follow the footsteps (khutuwat) of Satan﴾ meaning: his traces and his enticements. ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 209:

﴿Then if you slip﴾ turn away from the right course by [adopting] the prohibition of the Sabbath and the flesh of camels, ﴿after the clear proofs have come to you﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿then know that Allah is Mighty﴾ in His retribution; you cannot overpower Him, and nothing can overpower Him, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He has prescribed for you of His religion.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 210:

﴿Do they await﴾ means: do they await, i.e., those who refuse to enter Islam? (Hal) is an interrogative whose meaning is negation, i.e., these people await nothing in the Hereafter ﴿except that Allah should come to them﴾ with punishment ﴿in canopies of clouds﴾. The word ẓulal (canopies) is the plural of ẓullah, which is everything that shades you. The meaning is that the punishment comes in them and is more terrifying. ﴿And the angels﴾ means: the angels who were charged with punishing them ﴿and the matter is decided﴾, i.e., it is finished for them concerning what they were promised, by its being decreed upon them. ﴿And to Allah are all matters returned﴾ means: in terms of recompense, of reward and punishment.

Ask the Children of Israel: a question of rebuke, reproach and censure (as one says: "Ask him how often I admonished him and he did not accept"). ﴿How many clear signs did We give them?﴾ Such as the splitting of the sea, their deliverance from their enemy, the sending down of manna and quails, and other things. ﴿And whoever substitutes the favour of Allah after it has come to him﴾ meaning: the blessing Allah bestowed upon them, the knowledge concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ), but they substituted it and altered it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 212:

﴿Adorned for those who disbelieve is the life of this world﴾, that is, the leaders of the Jews. ﴿So they are preoccupied with it and seek it, for they desire nothing other than it﴾. ﴿And they mock those who believe﴾, that is, the poor among the Emigrants (muhajirun). ﴿But those who fear God﴾ from polytheism, and they are these poor ones, ﴿will be above them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, because they are in Paradise, which is elevated, while the disbelievers are in the Fire, which is an abyss (hawiyah). ﴿And God provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾. He means: the wealth of Qurayzah and al-Nadir will come to them without reckoning and without fighting, but with the easiest and most effortless thing.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 213:

﴿Mankind was one community﴾ in the time of Abraham, peace be upon him, all of them disbelievers. ﴿Then God sent the prophets﴾, Abraham and others, ﴿and sent down with them the Book﴾, and "the Book" is a generic noun, ﴿with the truth﴾, with justice and truthfulness, ﴿to judge between people﴾, i.e., the Book judges ﴿concerning that over which they differed. And none differed concerning it except those who were given it, after the clear proofs had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves﴾. That is: and none differed concerning the matter of Muhammad after the proofs had become clear to them, out of insolence (baghy) and envy, except the Jews who were given the Book. This is because the polytheists, although they differed concerning the matter of Muhammad, peace be upon him, did not act this way out of insolence and envy, and the clear proofs concerning the matter of Muhammad, peace be upon him, did not come to them as they came to the Jews; so the Jews are singled out in this respect. ﴿Then God guided those who believed﴾ to ﴿knowledge of﴾ ﴿what they differed over of the truth, by His permission﴾, by His knowledge and His will concerning them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 214:

﴿Do you think that you will enter Paradise﴾ It was revealed concerning the poor among the Emigrants (muhajirun) when hardship bore down upon them, because they had left (Makkah) without wealth. So God said to them, that is, to these Emigrants: Do you think that you will enter Paradise without trial or adversity? ﴿And not yet has there come to you﴾ that is, has not come to you ﴿the example of those who passed away﴾ that is, the like of the ordeal of those who went before ﴿before you﴾ that is, and there has not befallen you the like of what befell them, so that you would be patient as they were patient. ﴿They were touched by misfortune﴾ hardship (al-ba'sa') ﴿and adversity﴾ illness and hunger (al-ju', al-ju'), ﴿and were shaken﴾ that is, they were stirred by all kinds of trial, ﴿until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of God?"﴾ that is, when they were slow to receive victory. Then God said: ﴿Unquestionably, the help of God is near﴾ that is, I am the helper of My friends without doubt.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 215:

﴿They ask you what they should spend.﴾ It was revealed concerning ʿAmr ibn al-Jamuh, who was an elderly man and had great wealth. He asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "What should we spend from our wealth, and where should we place it?" So this verse was revealed. Many of the exegetes said: This was before the obligation of zakat. When zakat was made obligatory, zakat abrogated (naskh) this verse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 216:

﴿Fighting has been prescribed for you﴾: it was made obligatory and required of you, the jihad. ﴿And it is hateful to you﴾: meaning, it is a hardship upon you, because of what it entails for the self and wealth. ﴿But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you﴾: because in military campaign (ghazw) there is one of the two best outcomes (al-husnayayn): either victory and spoils, or martyrdom and Paradise. ﴿And perhaps you love a thing﴾: meaning, remaining behind from the campaign. ﴿And it is bad for you﴾: because of what it contains of humiliation, poverty, and the deprivation of spoils and reward. ﴿And Allah knows﴾ what holds your interests, so hasten to what He commands you, even if it is difficult for you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 217:

﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it.﴾ It was revealed concerning an expedition (*sariyyah*, a small military detachment) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent. They fought the polytheists while Rajab had begun, and they did not know it. The polytheists considered the shedding of blood in Rajab a grave matter, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿They ask you﴾, meaning the polytheists; and it was said: they are the Muslims. ﴿About the sacred month, about fighting in it.﴾ That is: and about fighting in it. ﴿Say: Fighting in it is a great (sin).﴾ Then he began and said: ﴿And barring/hindering﴾ and preventing ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, that is, from His obedience, meaning: the polytheists barred the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions from the Sacred House in the year of Hudaybiyyah. ﴿And disbelief in Him﴾, in Allah, ﴿and in the Sacred Mosque﴾, that is: and barring from the Sacred Mosque. ﴿And expelling its people﴾, that is: the people of the Mosque, meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions when they were expelled from Makkah. ﴿From it, is greater﴾ and graver in burden ﴿in the sight of Allah. And persecution﴾, that is: and polytheism, ﴿is greater than killing﴾, meaning: the killing by the expedition of the polytheists in Rajab. ﴿And they will not cease﴾, meaning the polytheists, ﴿fighting you until they turn you back from your religion﴾ to disbelief ﴿if they are able. And whoever of you reverts from his religion﴾ Islam, that is, returns and dies in disbelief, ﴿then those — their deeds have become void﴾ (their deeds were nullified).

Then these members of the expedition said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "We have struck the people in Rajab; do we hope that we will have the reward of those who strive in the way of Allah?" So Allah the Exalted revealed:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 218:

﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who emigrated﴾, who parted from their clans and homelands, ﴿and strove﴾ against the polytheists ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, in support of the religion of Allah. ﴿Those hope for the mercy of Allah, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. He forgave this raiding party (sariyya) what they had not known, and had mercy on them. Today there is a consensus (ijmāʿ) that fighting the polytheists is permissible in all the months, both the sacred and the non-sacred.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 219:

﴿They ask you about wine and gambling.﴾ It was revealed concerning ʿUmar, Muʿadh, and Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with them. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Give us a ruling about wine and gambling, for they take away the intellect and strip away wealth." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed His words: ﴿They ask you about wine.﴾ Wine is every intoxicant that mixes with the intellect and covers it. ﴿And gambling﴾ means al-qimar (games of chance). ﴿Say: In both is great sin.﴾ That is, the sin resulting from them, because of the quarreling, the reviling, the speaking of obscenity and falsehood, and other such things that they involve. ﴿And benefits for people.﴾ That is the wealth they gained from selling wine and trading in it, and the pleasure of drinking it. The benefit of gambling is what is won through it, and the poor are helped by it. Then He explained that the sin resulting from them is greater than their benefit, so He said: ﴿But their sin is greater than their benefit.﴾ This verse is not the one that prohibits wine and gambling; rather, the prohibition is in the verse in Surat al-Maʾida, and this verse was revealed before its prohibition.

﴿They ask you what they should spend.﴾ It was revealed concerning the question of ʿAmr ibn al-Jamuh, when Allah revealed His words: ﴿Whatever you spend should go to parents and relatives.﴾ He repeated the question and asked about the amount to be spent, so Allah revealed His words: ﴿Say: The surplus.﴾ That is, what remains of wealth after one's dependents are provided for. After the revelation of this verse, a man would take from his earnings what sufficed him and spend the rest, until zakat (obligatory alms) was prescribed. Then the verse of zakat in Surat Bara'a abrogated (naskh) this verse, and every charity they were commanded to give before zakat was abrogated as well.

﴿Thus⦆ means: like His explanation regarding wine and gambling, or regarding spending. ﴿Allah makes clear to you the signs,﴾ so that you may reflect on the matters of this world and the Hereafter, and thus recognize the superiority of the Hereafter over this world.

The Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 220:

﴿And they ask you about the orphans.﴾ In the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance), the Arabs were severe regarding the matter of the orphan: they would not eat with him, and they considered it an ill omen to mix with their property. So when Islam came, they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. And His saying: ﴿Say: Setting things right for them is best.﴾ Meaning: setting right their property without taking a wage is best and greater in reward. ﴿And if you mix with them﴾ you associate with them in their property and mix it with your property, so that you take from their property as a recompense for your management of their affairs. ﴿Then they are your brothers.﴾ That is: they are your brothers, and brothers help one another and each may take something from the other's property. ﴿And Allah knows the one who corrupts﴾ their property ﴿from the one who sets it right.﴾ So fear Allah regarding the property of the orphan, and do not make your mixing with them a means to corrupting their property and consuming it without right. ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have made it hard for you﴾ He would have constricted you and made you sinful for mixing with them. Its meaning is a reminder of the blessing of ease. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty﴾ in His dominion ﴿Wise﴾ in what He has commanded.

Revealed concerning Abu Murthad al-Ghanawi. He had a polytheist female companion (khalilah), and when he embraced Islam he asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Is it permissible for him to marry her?" So God revealed this verse: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾. Here "polytheistic women" is general, covering every woman who disbelieves in the Prophet (ﷺ). By this verse God prohibited marrying them. Then He made an exception for free women of the People of the Book (al-kitabiyyat) by the verse in al-Ma'idah, so the marriage of a bondwoman who is a People of the Book remains prohibited.

﴿And a believing slave-girl﴾. Revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Rawahah. He had a believing slave-girl, whom he freed and then married. Some people criticized him and offered him a free polytheistic woman, so this verse was revealed. And His words: ﴿even if she pleases you﴾ means because of her wealth and beauty.

﴿And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe﴾. It is not permissible under any circumstances to marry a Muslim woman to a polytheist.

﴿Those﴾, that is, the polytheists, ﴿invite to the Fire﴾, that is, to deeds that bring about the Fire.

﴿But God invites to Paradise and forgiveness﴾, that is, to deeds that bring about Paradise and forgiveness, ﴿by His permission﴾, by His command. The meaning is: by His commands He invites you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 222:

﴿And they ask you about menstruation.﴾ (The exegetes mentioned that the Arabs, when a woman menstruated, would not eat with her, nor drink with her, nor share a house with her, as the Magians did.) So Abu al-Dahdah asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "O Messenger of Allah, how should we deal with women when they menstruate?" Then this verse was revealed. Al-mahid: the menstruation (al-hayd). ﴿Say: It is an injury (adha),﴾ i.e., filth (qadhar) and blood. ﴿So keep away from women during menstruation,﴾ i.e., from having intercourse with them when they menstruate. ﴿And do not approach them﴾ i.e., do not have intercourse with them ﴿until they have purified themselves (yatahharna),﴾ i.e., until they have washed (yaghtasilna). Whoever reads ﴿yathurna﴾ with the light pronunciation, meaning: the blood stops from them, that is, purity is attained, which is the ritual bath (al-ghusl). ﴿And when they have purified themselves (tatahharna),﴾ i.e., have washed, ﴿then go to them (fa'tuhunna),﴾ i.e., have intercourse with them ﴿from where Allah has commanded you,﴾ i.e., by avoiding it during menstruation, which is the vagina. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant (al-tawwabin)﴾ from sins, ﴿and those who purify themselves (al-mutatahhirin)﴾ with water from minor and major ritual impurities.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 223:

﴿Your wives are a tilth for you (ḥarth lakum)﴾, that is: a field of cultivation and a place of sowing for offspring. ﴿So go to your tilth however you wish (anná shi'tum)﴾, that is: in whatever manner you wish and from whichever direction you wish, provided that it is in one orifice (ṣimām wāḥid). So this verse was revealed as a refutation of the Jews. The Muslims had said: "We approach women while they are crouching, standing, or lying on their backs, and from in front of them and from behind them, provided the place of entry is one and the same." The Jews said: "You are nothing but like cattle. We approach them in one posture only. We find in the Torah that every form of intercourse other than lying on the back is impure (dans) in the sight of God." So God refuted the Jews. ﴿And send ahead for yourselves (qaddimū li-anfusikum)﴾, that is: act for God in what He loves and is pleased with. ﴿And fear God (wa-ttaqū Allāh)﴾ regarding what He has set as limits for you concerning intercourse and the matter of the menstruating woman. ﴿And know that you will meet Him (mulāqūhu)﴾, that is: you will return to Him. ﴿And give good tidings to the believers (wa-bashshir al-mu'minīn)﴾ who fear Him and beware of disobeying Him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 224:

﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾, i.e., do not make the oath by Allah, glorified is He, a barrier preventing you from righteousness and piety, by deliberately taking oaths so that you may use them as excuses. It was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha, who swore that he would not speak to his brother-in-law (khatan) nor intervene between him and an opponent of his. He kept saying: "I have sworn that I will not do it, so it is not lawful for me [to do otherwise]." And His statement ﴿that you be righteous﴾, i.e., in [the matter of] not being righteous, or for the purpose of averting that you be righteous. It is permissible that His statement ﴿that you be righteous﴾ is a beginning (mubtada') whose predicate (khabar) is omitted, with the meaning: "that you be righteous, and God-conscious, and reconcile between people, is better," i.e., righteousness and piety are better. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾: He hears your oaths and knows what you intend by them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 225:

﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾, that is: what the tongue utters without any binding intention or purpose, serving merely as a filler in speech, such as the saying of one who says: "No, by Allah," and "Yes, by Allah." It was also said: the "lagw" (idle or unintended) oath is the oath for which expiation is made, and it was called "lagw" because the expiation removes the sin arising from it. ﴿But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾, that is: what you resolve and intend. According to the second view regarding the idle oath, its meaning is: but He will hold you accountable for your resolve not to do good, and for using your oaths as a pretext in that, saying that you had sworn. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾, He delays punishment from the disbelievers and the disobedient.

﴿For those who swear off their wives﴾, that is, who swear not to have intercourse with them. ﴿A waiting period of four months﴾: God Most High set the term for this at four months. When this period has passed, they must either divorce or resume intercourse; if they refuse both, the ruler (al-hakim) divorces on their behalf. ﴿And if they return﴾, that is, they go back on what they swore, namely by intercourse, ﴿then surely God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: He forgives him for what he has done. (And he is bound by the expiation for an oath.)

And if they are resolved upon divorce (﴿وإن عزموا الطلاق﴾), that is: they divorce and do not return to the marital relationship by intercourse (﴿ولم يفيؤوا بالوطء﴾), then indeed ﴿Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of what they say, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of what they do.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 228:

﴿And the divorced women﴾ i.e., those released from the bonds of husbands, meaning: those who have reached puberty and have been consummated with, not pregnant, because the verse explains their ʿiddah (waiting period). ﴿shall wait by themselves for three qurūʾ﴾ i.e., three periods of purity (ṭuhr), meaning: they shall await the completion of a period of three purities, until three purities have passed over them. And it was said: three menstrual periods (ḥayḍ). ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs﴾ meaning: the child, so that they do not nullify the husband's right of return (rajʿah). ﴿If they believe in Allah and the Last Day.﴾ This is a stern warning to them against concealing that. ﴿And their husbands have more right to take them back﴾ i.e., their husbands, ﴿in that﴾ — in the term during which they were commanded to wait — ﴿if they desire reconciliation﴾, not harm. ﴿And they have rights similar to those over them, according to what is reasonable﴾ i.e., women have over men rights similar to what men have over them, of what is right, according to what is reasonable, i.e., according to what Allah has commanded regarding the man's right over the woman. ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾ meaning: because of the dowry they have paid and the wealth they have spent. ﴿And Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾, He commands as He wills and tests as He loves.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 229:

﴿The divorce is twice﴾ The divorce of the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period) was not limited to any number, so Allah restricted divorce to three. He mentioned two in this verse and mentioned the third in the other verse, which is His saying:

﴿And if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that﴾ ... (the verse). It was also said: the meaning in the verse is that divorce in which the husband has the right of return (raj'ah) is twice.

﴿Then retain her in kindness﴾ meaning: if he takes her back after the two divorces, then he must retain her in accordance with what Allah the Exalted has commanded. ﴿Or release her with good treatment﴾ and this is that he leaves her until she becomes separated by the completion of the waiting period ('iddah) and does not take her back out of harm. ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾ It is not permissible for the husband to take from his wife anything of what he gave her as dower (mahr) in order to divorce her, except in khul' (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation), and this is His saying ﴿except when both fear﴾ that is: know ﴿that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. The meaning is: if the woman fears that she will disobey Allah regarding her husband out of hatred for him, and the husband fears that if his wife does not obey him he will wrong her, then it is lawful for him to take ransom (fidyah) from her if she offers it. ﴿And if you fear﴾ O rulers and judges ﴿that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾ meaning: the spouses ﴿then there is no blame upon them for what she gives up therewith﴾ — there is no blame on the woman for what she gives, nor on the man for what he takes. ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾ meaning: what He has prescribed of the laws of the religion.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 230:

﴿Then if he divorces her﴾, meaning: the husband who divorced her twice, ﴿then she is not lawful to him﴾, the woman divorced three times, ﴿after﴾, that is: after the third pronouncement of divorce, ﴿until she marries another husband﴾, other than the one who divorced her, (and has intercourse with her). ﴿Then if he divorces her﴾, that is: the second husband, ﴿there is no blame upon them both if they return to each other﴾ in a new marriage contract, ﴿if they think﴾, that is: if they know and are certain, ﴿that they will keep within the limits of Allah﴾, meaning what Allah has made clear of the right of each of them over the other.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 231:

﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term﴾ i.e., they approach the end of their waiting period (ʿidda). ﴿then retain them in kindness﴾ i.e., take them back with witnesses to the return (rajʿa) and a contract for it, not by intercourse, as Abu Hanifa says. ﴿or release them with kindness﴾ i.e., leave them until their waiting period ends, and they will be more entitled to themselves. ﴿And do not retain them to harm them﴾ i.e., do not take them back in order to harm them while you have no need of them. ﴿so that you may transgress﴾ against them by prolonging the waiting period. ﴿And whoever does that﴾ of transgression ﴿has certainly wronged himself﴾, harming his own soul and committing sin between himself and Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And do not take the signs of Allah in mockery﴾. A man in the Jahiliyya would divorce and say, "I divorced [her] while I was joking," and then return to her, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾ by Islam, ﴿and what He has sent down to you of the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and wisdom﴾, the admonitions of the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 232:

﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term﴾ — meaning their waiting period (ʿiddah) has ended — ﴿then do not prevent them﴾ — do not hinder them — ﴿from marrying their husbands﴾ — in a new marriage; that is, those who had been their husbands. It was revealed concerning the sister of Maʿqil ibn Yasar, whom her husband divorced. When her waiting period had ended, he came proposing to her again, but Maʿqil refused to let her marry him and prevented her by his right of guardianship (wilayah). ﴿When they agree among themselves in a proper manner﴾ — with a lawful contract and a permissible dowry (mahr). ﴿That﴾ — meaning, the command of Allah to refrain from ʿadl (preventing) — ﴿is an admonition for whoever among you believes in Allah and the Last Day. That is more virtuous﴾ — meaning, refraining from preventing is better — ﴿for you and purer﴾ — and more pure for your hearts from doubt, because if each of the two has a feeling of love in their heart, they cannot be trusted with one another. ﴿And Allah knows﴾ — what good there is for you in it.

﴿Wal-walidatu yurdi'na awladahunna﴾ (And mothers shall breastfeed their children). Its wording is that of a report, but its meaning is a command. It is a command of recommendation (*istihbab*), not of obligation (*ijab*). It means: mothers have the greater right to nurse over others, if they wish to do so. ﴿Hawlayni﴾ (for two years) ﴿kamilayn﴾ (complete). This is a fixing of the period to end disputes between the spouses if they disagree over the duration of nursing. This is indicated by His words ﴿liman arada﴾ (for whoever wishes), i.e., this determination and clarification ﴿li-man arada an yutimma al-rada'ah﴾ (for whoever wishes to complete the nursing). ﴿Wa-'ala al-mawludi lahu﴾ (And upon the one to whom the child is born), i.e., the father, ﴿rizquhunna wa-kiswatuhunna﴾ (is their provision and clothing), the provision and clothing of the mothers. The exegetes said: upon the husband is the provision and clothing of the divorced woman if she nurses the child. ﴿Bil-ma'ruf﴾ (in a reasonable manner), by what they recognize as just, as far as possible. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿La yukallifu nafsun illa wus'aha﴾ (No soul is burdened except according to its capacity). No soul is obligated except to what it can bear. ﴿La tudarra walidatun bi-waladiha﴾ (No mother shall be harmed because of her child). The child shall not be taken from her to another after she has agreed to nurse him and the child has become attached to her, nor shall she hand him over to his father after he has come to know her, harming him by doing so. This is His words: ﴿Wa-la mawludun lahu bi-waladihi﴾ (nor a father because of his child). ﴿Wa-'ala al-warithi mithlu dhalik﴾ (And upon the heir is the like of that). This is in succession to His words: ﴿Wa-'ala al-mawludi lahu rizquhunna wa-kiswatuhunna﴾, meaning: upon the heir of the child, who, if the child dies and has property, inherits it, is the like of what was upon his father during his life. By "the heir" he meant whoever is among his 'asabah (agnatic male relatives, those who inherit through the male line), whoever they may be among the men. ﴿Fa-in aradaa﴾ (If the two desire), i.e., the parents, ﴿fisalan﴾ (weaning) of the child ﴿'an taradin minhuma﴾ (by mutual consent) before the two years ﴿wa-tashawur﴾ (and mutual consultation) between them, ﴿fa-la junaha 'alayhima﴾ (there is no blame upon them both). ﴿Wa-in aradtum an tastardi'u awladakum﴾ (And if you wish to have your children nursed) by wet-nurses other than the mother, ﴿fa-la junaha 'alaykum﴾ (there is no blame upon you), ﴿idha sallamtum ma ataytum bil-ma'ruf﴾ (provided you hand over what you gave in a reasonable manner). i.e., provided you hand over to the mother her wage in proportion to what she nursed.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 234:

﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind﴾ i.e., who die, ﴿and leave wives behind﴾ and abandon (and leave behind) ﴿wives﴾, that is, women, ﴿who shall wait, keeping themselves, for four months and ten days﴾. The statement is a report with the meaning of a command. ﴿Four months and ten days﴾: this period is the ʿidda (the waiting period a woman observes after her husband's death or divorce) of a widow, unless she is pregnant. ﴿Then when they have reached their term﴾, meaning the ʿidda has ended, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, O guardians, ﴿for what they do with themselves in an honorable manner﴾, i.e., by marrying suitable husbands with the permission of the guardians. This is the explanation of ﴿al-maʿrūf﴾ here, because the one who gives herself in marriage the Prophet ﷺ called a fornicator (zāniya). This verse abrogates (naskh) the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿a provision for a year without expulsion﴾, and so on to the end of the verse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 235:

﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you hint at﴾ meaning: what you say without explicit declaration, which is to include in speech an indication of what one intends. ﴿Of proposal to women﴾ meaning: seeking to marry them during their ʿiddah, namely the woman whose husband has died. It is permissible to allude to proposing to her during the ʿiddah, which is to say to her, while she is in the ʿiddah: "Indeed you are beautiful, indeed you are virtuous, indeed you are righteous, and indeed among my intentions is to marry, and the like of that." ﴿Or you conceal within yourselves﴾ meaning: you keep secret and harbor, ﴿within yourselves﴾ of proposing to them and marrying them. ﴿Allah knows that you will remember them﴾ meaning: the proposal. ﴿But do not promise them secretly﴾ meaning: do not take from them a pledge that they will not marry anyone other than you. ﴿Except that you say a known saying﴾ meaning: allusion to the proposal as we have mentioned. ﴿And do not determine the tie of marriage﴾ meaning: do not validate the marriage contract ﴿until the decreed term reaches its end﴾ meaning: until the prescribed ʿiddah is completed. ﴿And know that Allah knows what is in your souls﴾ meaning: He is aware of what is in your hearts. ﴿So beware of Him﴾ meaning: fear Him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 236:

﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or specified for them a dower.﴾ It was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar who married a woman, did not specify a dower for her, and then divorced her before he had touched her. So God, exalted is He, informed that a marriage contract without a dower is permissible. Its meaning: there is no claim for the women against you if you divorce them before the consummation (al-masis) and before a dower (al-fard bi-sadaq) is fixed, nor any maintenance (nafaqa). And His saying: ﴿or specify for them an obligation﴾, that is: make a dower obligatory for them. ﴿And provide for them﴾, that is: give them provision and give them from your wealth what they may enjoy. So a woman who is divorced before a dower is specified and before consummation is entitled to the provision (mut'a) by the consensus of the scholars, and she has no dower. ﴿The wealthy man⁠⁠ ﴾ (al-muwassi'), that is: the rich man who is in ample circumstances according to his wealth, ﴿according to his means﴾, that is: according to his capacity. ﴿And the poor man⁠⁠ ﴾ (al-muqtir), who is in straitened circumstances due to his poverty, according to his capacity. The highest of it is a servant, the middle of it is a garment, and the least of it is the least of his wealth, a coin. Al-Shafi'i said: the good (husn) is thirty dirhams. ﴿A provision﴾, that is: provide for them a provision ﴿in a fair manner﴾, by what you recognize as moderate and within capacity. ﴿A duty⁠⁠ ﴾, obligatory, ﴿upon the good-doers﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 237:

﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, but after you have set a dowry for them, then half of what you have prescribed [is due]﴾. This refers to a divorced woman after a dowry has been named and before consummation (al-dukhul). God, exalted is He, ruled that she receives half the dowry, and this is His saying: ﴿then half of what you have prescribed﴾, meaning: the obligation is half of what you have prescribed. ﴿Unless they forgo﴾, meaning: the women, that is, unless they leave off that half and do not demand it from their husbands. ﴿Or he in whose hand is the marriage tie forgoes﴾, meaning: the husband does not reclaim any part of the dowry, and so he leaves her the full dowry he has paid, as a good deed. ﴿And that you forgo is nearer to piety﴾ is addressed to both men and women. ﴿Nearer to piety﴾ means more conducive to avoiding acts of disobedience to God, because this forgoing is recommended (nadb); when a person undertakes something recommended, it is known that, since it is not obligatory, it is more firmly acted upon. ﴿And do not forget graciousness between you﴾, meaning: do not neglect that some of you show favour to others. This is a command to both the husband and the wife to show favour and kindness.

Guard strictly the prayers, by performing them at their appointed times, and the middle prayer, that is, the dawn prayer, because it lies between the two night prayers and the two day prayers; he singled it out for mention for emphasis. And stand before Allah in devotion, obedient.

﴿Then if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾. That is: if you cannot perform the prayer fulfilling its due, then pray on foot, on your feet, ﴿or riding﴾ on the backs of your beasts, and this is in the case of pursuit and close combat. ﴿Then when you are secure, remember God﴾. That is: pray the five prayers complete with their rights, ﴿as He taught you what you did not know﴾, as He prescribed them for you at their appointed times.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 240:

﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind—let them bequeath for their wives﴾ a bequest, ﴿for their wives,﴾ that is, for their women. This was at the beginning of Islam: a wife had no inheritance from her husband, and it was incumbent upon the husband to bequeath to her a year's maintenance (nafaqah). So the heirs would maintain her for a year. The year was a binding obligation upon her, to remain patient and refrain from remarrying, but she had the choice: if she wished, she could observe the waiting period (iddah) in the husband's house, and if she wished, she could leave before the year was over, and her maintenance would lapse. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿a provision until the year, without being turned out.﴾ That is, provide for them a provision, meaning maintenance, ﴿without being turned out,﴾ that is, without the heirs expelling them. ﴿But if they leave, then there is no blame upon you﴾ O guardians of the deceased, for discontinuing their maintenance and for not preventing them from presenting themselves for marriage and adorning themselves for husbands. This is His words: ﴿for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable.﴾ All of this was abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of inheritance and the verse of the waiting period of a widow (iddat al-mutawaffa 'anha zawjuha).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 241:

﴿And for divorced women is a provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the righteous.﴾ When Allah the Exalted mentioned the provision for the divorced woman in His saying, ﴿a duty upon the doers of good﴾, a man among the Muslims said: "If I wish, I will do it, and if I do not wish to do it, I will not do it." So Allah the Exalted made it obligatory upon the righteous (al-muttaqun), those who guard themselves against polytheism (al-shirk).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 242:

﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses﴾. Allah likens the clarification that comes now to the clarification that preceded it in the rulings He had mentioned.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 243:

﴿Have you not considered those who left their homes⁠—﴾ Have you not known? Has your knowledge not reached these people? They were a people of the Children of Israel who left their town fleeing from the plague, until they came down in a valley. So God caused them all to die, and this is His saying: ﴿out of fear of death﴾, meaning: for fear of death. ﴿So God said to them, "Die," and then He brought them back to life.﴾ God rebuked them for their fleeing from death, so He caused them to die as a punishment for them, then He raised them up so that they might complete the remainder of their terms. ﴿Indeed, God is bounteous toward the people﴾, meaning: He is gracious toward them by giving them life after their death.
Fight in the way of God. (He) urges the believers to fighting. ﴿And know that God is All-Hearing﴾ of what the one making excuses says, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of what he conceals. So beware of making excuses.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 245:

﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan﴾ means: who is it that will act as a lender, by giving from his wealth and receiving back many times what he gave? This is an invitation from Allah, exalted is He, to works of righteousness. ﴿And Allah withholds and grants abundance﴾ means: He withholds provision from whom He wills, and He expands it for whom He wills.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 246:

﴿Have you not considered the chiefs (al-mala') of the Children of Israel?﴾ That is: the group (al-jama'ah). ﴿When they said to a prophet of theirs, "Appoint for us a king (malik) that we may fight in the way of Allah."﴾ They asked their prophet, Ushmuwil (Samuel), peace be upon him, for a king through whom their word would be united and their affairs would be set right in fighting their enemy. This is what is meant by His words: ﴿"that we may fight in the way of Allah."﴾ ﴿He said﴾ to them, that prophet: ﴿"Is it likely that if fighting is prescribed for you, you will not fight?"﴾ That is: perhaps you will shrink back from fighting. ﴿They said, "And what is [the matter] with us that we should not fight in the way of Allah?"﴾ That is: what prevents us from doing so? ﴿"And we have been expelled from our homes"﴾ ﴿"and"﴾ separated from ﴿"our children"﴾ by captivity and killing. When the matter has reached this point with us, fighting is necessary. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿"So when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them."﴾ They are those who crossed the river, and their mention will come.

[Wahidi's commentary on 2:247, continuing as given]

﴿And their prophet said to them, "Indeed, Allah has sent Talut (Saul) to you as king."﴾ That is: He has granted you what you asked for, namely the sending of a king. ﴿They said﴾: "How can he rule over us?" He was from one of the lowest houses of the Children of Israel and was not from the tribe of kingship, so they denied his kingship and said: ﴿"And we are more entitled to the kingship than he, and he has not been given abundance of wealth."﴾ That is: he was not given what kings use to acquire kingship. ﴿He said﴾, the Prophet: ﴿"Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you"﴾ (meaning: selected him) for kingship, ﴿"and has increased him broadly in knowledge and physique."﴾ Talut was at that time the most knowledgeable man among the Children of Israel, and the most handsome and the most complete in build. Al-basta means increase in everything. ﴿"And Allah gives His kingdom to whom He wills."﴾ It is not by inheritance. ﴿"And Allah is All-Encompassing"﴾ That is: abundant in bounty, provision and mercy. So they asked their prophet for a sign of Talut's kingship, and so—

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 248:

﴿And their Prophet said to them: "Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that there will come to you the Ark (al-tabut)."﴾ It was a chest (tabut) that Allah the Exalted had sent down to Adam (peace be upon him), in which were the images (suwar) of the prophets (peace be upon them). The Children of Israel used to seek victory through it over their enemy. Then the Amalekites overpowered them and seized the Ark. When they asked their Prophet for a clear sign (al-bayyinah) of Talut's kingship, he said: "Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that Allah will return the Ark to you." So the angels carried the Ark and placed it in the house of Talut.

As for His words, ﴿In it is tranquility (sakinah) from your Lord﴾, meaning: a state of calm (tuma'ninah), by which their hearts were reassured. Wherever the Ark was, they would settle there, and this was by the command of Allah the Exalted.

﴿And a remainder of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun left behind﴾, meaning: the two of them had left it. The remainder was the sandals of Musa, his staff, the turban of Harun, and a qafiz (measure) of the manna (al-manna) that used to descend upon them.

﴿Carried by the angels﴾, meaning: the Ark.

﴿Indeed, in that is a sign﴾, meaning: in the return of the Ark to you is a sign that Allah has made Talut king over you.

﴿If you are believers﴾, meaning: if you are affirmers of the truth (musaddiqin).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 249:

﴿Then when Talut set out with the armies﴾ i.e., he led them out from the place where they were to fight the enemy. ﴿He said﴾ to them, Talut: ﴿Indeed, Allah is going to test you﴾ i.e., He will try you and deal with you as one who tests, ﴿with a river﴾ i.e., the river of Palestine, so that the one who is sincere and has the intention of jihad may be distinguished from the excuse-maker, ﴿so whoever drinks from it﴾ i.e., from its water, ﴿is not of me﴾ i.e., is not of my people, ﴿and whoever does not taste it﴾ does not partake of it, ﴿indeed he is of me, except one who scoops with his hand a handful﴾ i.e., once only; i.e., he takes from it with a jar, a waterskin, or the like, one time. Talut said to them: whoever drinks from the river and drinks much has disobeyed Allah, and whoever scoops a handful with his hand, that suffices him. So they rushed upon the river after intense thirst, and most of them fell into the river and drank excessively. These ones became cowardly about meeting the enemy, while a people few in number obeyed and did not exceed the scooping. Their hearts were strengthened and they crossed the river. This is His saying: ﴿So they drank from it, except a few of them﴾. They were three hundred and some ten men. ﴿Then when he crossed it﴾ i.e., the river, ﴿he and those who believed with him, they said﴾ meaning: those who drank and opposed the command of Allah the Exalted: ﴿We have no power today against Goliath and his armies.﴾ ﴿Said﴾ meaning: the few who scooped, and they are ﴿those who are certain﴾ i.e., who know ﴿that they will meet Allah﴾ i.e., will return to Him: ﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah. And Allah is with the patient﴾ with help and victory.

"When they went out to Goliath and his soldiers," that is, came forth against them to fight, "they said: Our Lord, pour out upon us patience (ṣabr) and make our feet firm," by strengthening our hearts.

﴿So they routed them﴾, driving them back and breaking them, ﴿by the permission of God﴾, by His decree and His determination. ﴿And David killed Goliath﴾, the Prophet, who was in the army of the Children of Israel, killed ﴿Jalut﴾, the disbeliever. ﴿And God gave him the kingdom﴾ (God gave David the kingship of the Children of Israel) ﴿and wisdom﴾, that is, He gathered for him kingship and prophethood. ﴿And taught him of what He willed﴾: the craft of making armor and the speech of birds. ﴿And had God not repelled some people by means of others﴾: had God not repelled the disbelievers by means of the armies of the Muslims, the polytheists would have prevailed over the earth, killed the believers, and ruined the lands and the mosques.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 252:

﴿Those are the verses of Allah﴾ meaning: these verses which I have told you about are the verses of Allah, that is, the signs of His oneness. ﴿And indeed you are among the messengers﴾ meaning: you are among those whose accounts I have related to you.

These are the messengers: We (God) made some of them superior to others. That is, We did not make them equal in virtue, even though they were equal in carrying out the mission. Among them is the one to whom God spoke, namely Musa (Moses), peace be upon him. And He raised some of them in rank, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), who was sent to all people.

We gave Isa (Jesus), son of Maryam (Mary), clear proofs and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit. Its explanation has already passed.

Had God willed, those who came after them would not have fought one another after clear proofs had come to them. That is, after the messengers, after the clear proofs had become evident to them. But they differed: some of them believed, remaining steadfast in their faith, and some of them disbelieved, like the Christians after the Messiah. They differed and became sects, then they waged war against one another.

Had God willed, they would not have fought. He repeated the mention of the will with regard to their fighting, as a refutation of whoever claimed that they did this of their own accord, not by a decree from God. But God does what He wills: He grants success to whomever He wills by His grace, and forsakes whomever He wills by His justice.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 254:

﴿O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided for you﴾ That is: the obligatory zakat. It was also said: he intended spending in jihad. ﴿before there comes a Day in which there is no trade, nor friendship, nor intercession﴾ meaning: the Day of Resurrection. Meaning: on that day no ransom or redemption will be accepted. ﴿Nor friendship﴾ nor companionship. ﴿Nor intercession﴾ He stated the negation of intercession in general terms, because He meant the disbelievers, that these things will not benefit them. Do you not see that He said: ﴿And the disbelievers, they are the wrongdoers﴾? That is: they are the ones who placed the command of Allah in other than its proper place.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 255:

﴿Allah—there is no god but He, the Ever-Living (al-Hayy), the Self-Subsisting (al-Qayyum)﴾: the one who lasts forever, the one who is in charge of managing the affairs of creation in their creation and their provision. ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾: drowsiness (sunnah) is the first stage of sleep, and sleep (nawm) is the heavy overwhelming of the senses. ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾: in ownership and in creation. ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ That is: no one can intercede with Him except by His command, refuting the claim of the disbelievers that the idols would intercede for them. ﴿He knows what is before them﴾ of the affairs of this world, ﴿and what is behind them﴾ of the affairs of the Hereafter. ﴿And they encompass nothing of His knowledge﴾ That is: they know nothing of what Allah knows ﴿except what He wills﴾, except what Allah has informed the prophets of and made them aware of. ﴿His Seat (kursi) extends over the heavens and the earth﴾: that is, it bears them and is strong enough for them, meaning His dominion and His authority. It has also been said that the Kursi is itself the thing in question, and that it encompasses the heavens and the earth in its greatness. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that the Kursi is His knowledge. ﴿And their preservation does not tire Him﴾: that is, it does not burden or weigh on Him, ﴿the preservation of them both﴾, that is, the preservation of the heavens and the earth. ﴿And He is the Most High (al-ʿAli)﴾ in power and in the far-reaching of His authority, above likenesses and equals, ﴿the Most Great (al-ʿAzim)﴾, great in standing.

﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾ after the Arabs embraced Islam, because they had been compelled to accept Islam. So the jizya (poll tax) was not accepted from them, since they had been polytheists. When they embraced Islam, God the Exalted revealed this verse.

﴿The right course has become clear from error﴾: faith became distinguished from disbelief, and guidance from misguidance, through the abundance of proofs. ﴿Whoever disbelieves in the Taghut (the false deities, i.e. Satan and the idols)﴾ ﴿and believes in God﴾ and the Last Day, ﴿has grasped the most trustworthy handhold﴾: i.e., he has held fast (tamassaka) to it. He has tied for himself a firm bond, which is faith and the declaration of the two testimonies (kalimat al-shahadatayn). ﴿There is no breaking of it﴾: i.e., there is no severing of it. ﴿And God is Hearing﴾ of your supplication, O Muhammad, regarding the conversion of the People of the Book. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) loved the conversion of the People of the Book who were around Madinah, and he would ask God for that. ﴿Knowing﴾ of your eagerness and striving.

Allah is the Ally (wali) of those who believe: that is, their Helper and the one who takes charge of their affairs. ﴿He brings them out of the darknesses﴾ from disbelief and misguidance into faith and guidance. ﴿And those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., the Jews, ﴿their allies are the taghut﴾ meaning their leaders, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Huyayy ibn Akhtab. ﴿They bring them out of the light﴾ meaning from what they were upon of faith in Muhammad (ﷺ) before his being sent, ﴿into the darknesses﴾, into disbelief in him after his being sent.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 258:

﴿Have you not considered the one who argued﴾ disputed and contended ﴿with Abraham about his Lord﴾ when he said to him: "Who is your Lord?" ﴿because Allah had given him kingship﴾ i.e., the kingship that Allah had given him. He means: the arrogance of kingship led him to that, and he was Nimrod ibn Canaan. ﴿When Abraham said, "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death."﴾ The enemy of Allah said: ﴿"I give life and cause death."﴾ So Abraham countered him by the shared wording, without any act of giving life or causing death. When he confused the argument by saying, "I do that," Abraham presented him with a proof in which he could not say "I do that," namely His saying: ﴿Abraham said, "Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west." So the one who disbelieved was overwhelmed﴾ i.e., he was silenced and became mute.

﴿Or like one who passed by a town﴾ is a conjunction with the meaning, not the wording, as if he had said: "Have you not considered the one who argued, or like the one who passed by while he was a mighty one" ﴿over a town﴾, which is Iliya, ﴿and it was in ruins﴾, fallen and collapsed, ﴿upon its roofs﴾, meaning its ceilings. ﴿He said: How will God bring this to life﴾, meaning: From where will God bring this to life ﴿after its death﴾, restoring it after its ruin? He found it hard that God should do this, so God wished to show him a sign in himself concerning the revival of the town. ﴿So God caused him to die for a hundred years﴾. This is because he passed by this town on a donkey, with a skin of juice and a basket of figs. He tied up his donkey, and God caused him to fall asleep. When he slept, God, mighty and majestic, took his soul for a hundred years. When a hundred years had passed, God, exalted, revived him, and this is His saying: ﴿Then He raised him up﴾. ﴿He said: How long have you remained?﴾, meaning: How long have you stayed and remained here? ﴿He said: I have remained a day or part of a day. He said: Rather, you have remained a hundred years. So look at your food﴾, meaning the figs, ﴿and your drink﴾, meaning the juice, ﴿they have not spoiled﴾, meaning they had not changed or become rotten after a hundred years. He showed him the sign of his staying a hundred years through the decay of his donkey's bones. Then He said: ﴿And look at your donkey﴾, so he saw his donkey dead, its bones white and gleaming. ﴿And that We may make you a sign for the people﴾: the "and" is extra, and the meaning is: You remained a hundred years so that We may make you a sign for the people. His being a sign was that He raised him up young, with black hair and beard, while his grandchildren were gray-haired. ﴿And look at the bones﴾, meaning the bones of his donkey, ﴿how We raise them﴾, meaning how We bring them to life. It is said: God raised the dead (anshara). It is also read as ﴿nunshizuha﴾, meaning We lift them from the ground, and the rising (nushuz) of everything is its elevation. ﴿Then We clothe them with flesh. So when it became clear to him﴾, when he witnessed that, ﴿he said: I know that God is over all things capable﴾, meaning: I know with a knowledge that admits no doubt. Its interpretation is: I have now known by direct witnessing what I used to know only by report of the unseen.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 260:

﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead."﴾ This was because he saw a carcass on the seashore, which the birds of prey, the wild beasts and the creatures of the sea were feeding on. He reflected on how what had been scattered of it could be brought back together, and he wished to see that. So he asked Allah, exalted is He, to show him the giving of life to the dead. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do you not believe?﴾ Have you not already believed in that? ﴿He said, "Yes, but that my heart may be at rest."﴾ That is, through direct witnessing after belief in the unseen. ﴿He said, "Take four birds"﴾ a peacock, a vulture, a crow and a rooster. ﴿Then cut them into pieces (ṣurrahunna ilayka)﴾ That is, cut them up, as if He had said: take to yourself four birds and cut them up. ﴿Then place on every hill a portion of them﴾ Then he was commanded to mix their feathers and flesh, then to separate their parts by placing them on four hills. Abraham did that, and he kept their heads with him. Then he called them and said: "Come to me by Allah's permission." The parts of the birds began to fly toward one another until their parts were complete, and then they came back to their heads. This is His saying: ﴿Then call them, and they will come to you in haste.﴾ ﴿And know that Allah is Almighty﴾ nothing He wills can be prevented from Him, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He arranges. When He mentioned the evidence of His oneness through the clear signs brought by the messengers, He urged to jihad and spending in it, so He said:

﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of God﴾, i.e., the likeness of their charity and spending, ﴿is like a grain that has grown seven ears﴾. He means that He multiplies the one by seven hundred, and He made it like a grain that produces seven hundred grains. Its existence is not a condition of coining the parable (*darb al-mathal*, the striking of an illustrative example).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 262:

﴿Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah, then do not follow up what they have spent with reproach and injury...﴾ The verse continues. The reproach (al-mann) is that one says: "I have done good to so-and-so, supported him, and mended his condition," reminding of what he has done. ﴿Nor injury﴾ (al-adha) is that one mentions his kindness before someone the recipient does not like, and his standing over him (to receive it).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 263:

﴿A kind word﴾ means good speech and a gracious response to the one who asks. ﴿And forgiveness﴾ means overlooking the one who asks when he becomes insolent toward him in refusing him. ﴿Better than charity followed by injury﴾ means reproach and taunting the one who asks for having asked. ﴿And Allah is Rich﴾ above the charity of His servants, ﴿Forbearing﴾ in that He does not hasten punishment upon the one who reproaches.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 264:

﴿O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities [by reminders] of your generosity or [by] injury,﴾ that is, their reward, ﴿by reminders of generosity﴾, which is to remind the recipient of what one has given, ﴿and injury﴾, which is for the giver to reproach the one who receives. ﴿Like one who spends [his wealth] to be seen by the people﴾, that is, like the invalidation of one who gives out of showing off to people, and this is the hypocrite who gives in order to make others think he is a believer. ﴿So his example﴾, that is, the example of this hypocrite, ﴿is like the example of a smooth rock﴾, which is a bare, smooth stone, ﴿on which is dust, and then a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare [and hard]﴾, meaning a heavy downpour, ﴿leaving it smooth and bare﴾, shining and smooth. This is a parable that Allah, the Exalted, struck for the one who reminds of his generosity and for the hypocrite. That is to say: people see outwardly that these have deeds, just as dust is seen on this rock. But when the Day of Resurrection comes, all of it will vanish and be invalidated, just as the downpour removed what was on the smooth rock, so no one among the creation can retrieve that dust. Likewise these people, when they come before their Lord, will find nothing. This is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿They are not able to [gain] anything of what they have earned﴾, that is, to any reward for anything they have earned. ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾, meaning He does not make their recompense for their disbelief to be that He guides them.

(Then He struck an example for one who spends, seeking what is with Allah, and does not remind of his generosity or injure, and so He said:)

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 265:

﴿And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking the approval of Allah and for the firm establishment of their souls﴾ means: certainty and affirmation ﴿from themselves﴾ regarding the reward, unlike the hypocrite who does not believe in the reward. ﴿Like a garden on a height﴾, and rabwah (elevated ground) is what rises above the land, and it is more abundant in produce than the lowland (al-mustafil). ﴿Struck by heavy rain﴾, and wabl is the most intense rain. ﴿It yields its produce﴾ gave its yield, ﴿its food﴾ what is eaten from it, ﴿twofold﴾. That means it bore in one year what other land bears in two years. ﴿But if heavy rain does not strike it, then light rain (tall)﴾, and tall is the weak rain, ﴿and that is its state of blessing﴾. He says: just as this garden bears fruit in every condition and its owner is not disappointed, whether the rain is little or much, so Allah multiplies the reward of the believer's charity whether his expenditure is small or large. Then he establishes the parable of the one who shows off in spending and who falls short in obedience until he dies, with his words:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 266:

﴿Would any of you wish﴾ means: their likeness is like that of a man who had a garden, in which there were all kinds of fruits, ﴿and old age had overtaken him﴾, so he was weak in earning, and he had young children who could not benefit from it nor help him, ﴿and then a whirlwind﴾, which is a violent wind, ﴿containing fire struck it, and it was burned.﴾ So he lost it when he needed it most, at the time of advanced age, many dependents, and the childhood of his offspring, so he and his children remained helpless and bewildered, ﴿unable to do anything﴾ (to devise a plan). Thus Allah nullifies the deeds of the hypocrite and the one who shows off, so that for them there is no repentance and no pardon for their sins. ﴿Thus Allah makes clear﴾, like the clarification of these parables, ﴿Allah makes clear to you the signs﴾ concerning the matter of His oneness.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 267:

﴿O you who have believed, spend from the good things you have earned﴾. It was revealed concerning a people who used to give in charity the worst of their fruits and the most worthless of their wealth. By "the good things" (al-tayyibat) is meant here the best and choicest, "of what you have earned," i.e., from trade. ﴿And from what We have brought forth for you from the earth﴾, meaning: the grains upon which zakat is obligatory. ﴿And do not aim at the bad [therein] to spend from it﴾, i.e., do not intend to spend the bad. ﴿While you would not accept it except with closed eyes﴾, i.e., you would not take that bad thing, if it were given to you as a right owed to you, except by overlooking it and being lenient. In this is a clarification that the poor are partners of the owner of the wealth, and a partner does not take the inferior from the superior except with leniency.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 268:

﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty﴾, i.e., he frightens you with it, saying: Hold on to your wealth, for if you give charity you will become poor. ﴿And commands you to immorality﴾, i.e., to stinginess and withholding zakat. ﴿But Allah promises you﴾ that He will reward you for your charity with ﴿forgiveness﴾ of your sins, and that He will replace for you what you have spent.

﴿He gives wisdom to whomever He wills﴾: that is, the knowledge of the Qur'an and understanding of it. It is said: it is prophethood. ﴿And none will be reminded except those of understanding﴾: that is, none will take heed except those possessed of intellects.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 270:

﴿And whatever expenditure you spend﴾, i.e., you pay as zakat, ﴿or whatever vow you vow﴾, i.e., in voluntary charity, that is: you intend to give a charity, ﴿indeed Allah knows it﴾, He will reward for it, ﴿and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾. This is a threat for whoever spends in a manner not permitted to him, such as out of showing off, or in disobedience, or from property that was usurped.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 271:

﴿If you show your charity, it is good;﴾ they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "Is secret charity better, or public charity?" So this verse was revealed. The exegetes are agreed that this verse concerns voluntary charity (al-tatawwu'), not obligatory charity (al-fard), for the obligatory charity is better when it is shown openly. According to some of them, the verse is general, applying to every charity. As for His words, ﴿and He will remove from you some of your misdeeds﴾, meaning He will forgive them for you; and "min" (from) here is for emphasis and reinforcement.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 272:

﴿It is not upon you to guide them﴾ It was revealed when Qutayla, the mother of Asma' bint Abi Bakr, asked her daughter to give her something, while she was a polytheist. She refused and said: "I will not do so until I consult the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." Then this verse was revealed. The meaning is: it is not upon you to guide those who oppose you, so he withheld charity from them so that they would enter Islam. ﴿And whatever good you spend﴾ that is, wealth, ﴿it is for yourselves﴾ its reward. ﴿And you spend only seeking the face of God﴾ is a report, but what is meant is a command. It was also said that it is specific to the believers, meaning: God knows this about you. ﴿And whatever good you spend﴾ of wealth upon the poor among the People of the Suffa ﴿will be repaid to you﴾ that is, its reward will be paid to you in full. ﴿And you will not be wronged﴾ that is, you will not be deprived of anything from the reward of your deeds.

For the poor (lit. "to the poor"), i.e., these charities and expenditures mentioned earlier, who are confined ("ahsiru") — i.e., they have been restrained; they did this, restraining themselves, in the way of God, in jihad, meaning the poor among the Emigrants (muhajirun), who cannot travel ("darban") in the land, i.e., journey, not devoting themselves to seeking a livelihood, because they have bound themselves to the matter of jihad, and that prevented them from engaging in trade. God, exalted is He, urged the believers to spend on them. "The ignorant person thinks them rich because of their restraint" — he supposes them to be rich — "from [their] abstention" from asking. "You recognize them by their mark" — by their sign of humility, lowliness, and the trace of hardship. "They do not ask people insistently" — i.e., with persistence: if they had lunch, they would not ask for dinner, and if they had dinner, they would not ask for lunch.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 274:

﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day﴾ It was revealed concerning ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. He had four dirhams and owned no others. He gave one dirham in secret, one dirham openly, one dirham by night, and one dirham by day.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 275:

﴿Those who consume interest (al-riba)﴾ i.e., those who deal in it. By mentioning "consuming," he draws attention to other forms of dealing. ﴿Will not stand﴾ from their graves on the Day of Resurrection ﴿except as one stands whom Satan has driven to madness by touch﴾, i.e., afflicts with insanity ﴿from the touch﴾, i.e., from madness. This is because the one who consumes interest will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as a madman. ﴿That﴾ i.e., that which has befallen them ﴿is because they said, "Trade is only like interest"﴾. This is because the polytheists said: an increase over the principal after the due date of a debt is like the increase of profit at the outset of a sale. So Allah, exalted is He, refuted them, saying: ﴿But Allah has permitted trade and forbidden interest. So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord﴾, i.e., was admonished, ﴿and desists﴾ from consuming interest, ﴿for him is what has passed﴾, i.e., what he consumed of interest is not his to return, and he is not required to return what he took before the prohibition ﴿and his affair is up to Allah﴾, and Allah is the guardian of his affair. ﴿And whoever returns﴾ to considering interest lawful ﴿those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 276:

﴿Allah destroys usury﴾, that is: He diminishes it and removes its blessing, even if it is abundant, just as the moon is diminished. ﴿And He causes charities to grow﴾, He causes them to increase for their owner, just as one of you raises his young camel (fasil). ﴿And Allah does not love every ungrateful sinner﴾, one who disbelieves in the prohibition of usury, considering it lawful for himself. ﴿Sinful﴾, wicked by consuming it (persisting in it).

O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of the riba (interest), if you are believers.

It was revealed concerning al-ʿAbbas and ʿUthman, may Allah be pleased with them both, who had lent money on riba before its prohibition. When this verse was revealed, they heard it and obeyed, and took back their principal sums.

The meaning of the verse: the prohibition of whatever riba remains as a debt, and the obligation to take only the principal without any addition by way of riba. As for His words, ﴿if you are believers﴾, that is: whoever is a believer, this is his ruling.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 279:
