﴿Then if you do not do it﴾ — i.e., if you do not give up what remains of the riba (usury). ﴿Then be informed﴾ — i.e., know. ﴿Of war from Allah and His Messenger﴾ — i.e., be certain that by refusing to abandon it, you are at war with Allah and His Messenger. ﴿But if you repent﴾ — from riba. ﴿Then you have your principal; you do not wrong [others] by seeking increase﴾ — by demanding an excess. ﴿Nor are you wronged﴾ — by being given less than the principal.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 280:

﴿And if the debtor is in hardship﴾, i.e., if a debtor who is in hardship arises, ﴿then let there be a delay﴾, i.e., upon you is a delay, meaning postponement, ﴿until a time of ease﴾, until wealth and the availability of money. ﴿And that you remit [it as charity]﴾ to those in hardship, [forgiving] the principal, ﴿is better for you﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 281:

﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah﴾. That is: the Day of Resurrection, on which you will be brought back to Allah. ﴿Then every soul will be paid in full what it earned﴾, i.e., the recompense of the deeds it earned. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾, meaning they will not have anything diminished. When Allah, exalted is He, prohibited riba (usury), He permitted al-salam (advance sale) and said:

﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term﴾, i.e., when you deal with one another on credit, ﴿then write it down﴾. Allah, exalted is He, commanded that deferred rights be recorded in writing and witnessed, in His saying: ﴿And call two witnesses when you conclude a sale﴾, to preserve the wealth. Then this was abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of a earlier ruling by a later one) by His saying: ﴿But if one of you trusts another, let the one who is trusted fulfill his trust﴾, the verse. ﴿And let a scribe write it down between you﴾, between the creditor and the debtor, ﴿with justice﴾, with truth and fairness, and let him not add to or subtract from the amount or the term. ﴿And let not a scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him﴾, i.e., let him not refrain from doing so when he is commanded. This was an obligation from Allah upon the scribe and the witness, and it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿Let no scribe or witness be harmed﴾. Then He said: ﴿So let him write, as Allah has taught him﴾, i.e., as Allah has favored him with the ability to write. ﴿And let the one who owes the debt dictate﴾, i.e., the one who owes the debt should dictate, because he is the one against whom testimony is given, so he acknowledges it with his own tongue so that he knows what he owes. ﴿And let him not diminish anything from it﴾: he is commanded to acknowledge the amount of the wealth without any reduction. ﴿But if the one who owes the debt is foolish﴾ (i.e., the debt), a child, ﴿or weak﴾, incapable or feeble-minded, ﴿or unable to dictate himself﴾ because of muteness or an impediment in speech, ﴿then let his guardian dictate﴾, his heir or whoever stands in his place, ﴿with justice﴾, with truthfulness and right. ﴿And call to witness﴾, and have witnessed, ﴿two witnesses from among your men﴾, i.e., from among the people of your religious community, free adult males. And His saying: ﴿from among those whom you accept as witnesses﴾, i.e., from among people of merit and religion. ﴿So that if one of them errs﴾, forgets, ﴿the other may remind her﴾, of the testimony. ﴿And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called﴾ to bear witness or to give it. ﴿And do not be weary of writing it, whether it be small or large, up to its term﴾, up to the term of the right. ﴿That is more just﴾, more equitable, ﴿in the sight of Allah﴾ in His judgment, ﴿and more upright﴾, more conducive to uprightness, ﴿for testimony﴾, because the writing reminds the witnesses, so their testimony is more upright. ﴿And more likely to prevent doubt﴾, i.e., more likely that you will not doubt the amount of the right or the term. ﴿Except when it is a present trade﴾, that occurs, ﴿a present trade﴾, i.e., a trade in which goods and other things are present and exchanged on the spot, which is the meaning of His saying: ﴿that you conduct among yourselves﴾. This is because what is feared in deferred payment is secure in a sale of hand-to-hand exchange. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿There is no blame on you if you do not write it down; but call witnesses when you conclude a sale﴾. We have mentioned that this ruling has been abrogated, so it is not obligatory. ﴿And let no scribe or witness be harmed﴾. Allah, exalted is He, forbade the scribe and the witness from harm, which is for the scribe to add to, subtract from, or distort the record, and for the witness to testify to what he was not asked about, or to refrain from giving testimony. ﴿And if you do so﴾, any of this, ﴿then it is a transgression on your part﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 283:

﴿And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe﴾ — the verse. When there is no scribe, God, exalted is He, commands taking a pledge (rahn) so that it serves as a guarantee for the wealth, and this is His saying: ﴿then a pledge taken into possession﴾, i.e., then the guarantee is a pledge taken into possession. ﴿But if one of you trusts another﴾, i.e., does not fear his betrayal or his denial of the right. ﴿Then let him who is trusted discharge his trust﴾, i.e., the one entrusted with it, ﴿his trust, and let him fear God, his Lord﴾ by discharging the trust. ﴿And do not conceal testimony﴾ when you are called to establish it. ﴿Whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful﴾, i.e., wicked, ﴿his heart﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 284:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, (in the sense of) ownership, so He is the owner of their essences. ﴿And whether you reveal what is in your selves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it.﴾ When this was revealed, some of the Companions (ṣaḥāba) came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "We have been burdened with deeds we cannot bear. One of us may speak to himself with things he does not like to settle in his heart, and are we to be called to account for that?" The Prophet said: "Perhaps you are saying what the Children of Israel said: 'We hear and we disobey.' Rather say: 'We hear and we obey.'" So they said: "We hear and we obey." Then Allah the Exalted sent down relief through His words: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾. This verse abrogated (naskh) what came before it. It has also been said that this (verse) concerns concealing testimony and establishing it. As for His words ﴿Allah will bring you to account for it﴾, the meaning is that He will inform you of it and make you aware of it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 285:

﴿The Messenger believes﴾ the verse. When Allah the Exalted mentioned in this surah the rulings, the limits, the stories of the prophets, and the signs of His power, He concluded the surah by mentioning the affirmation of His Prophet, peace be upon him, and the believers, of all of that. ﴿We make no distinction between any of them﴾, meaning: they say, "We make no distinction between any of His messengers, as the People of the Book did, who believed in some of the messengers and disbelieved in others; rather, we combine them all in belief in them." ﴿And they say, "We hear"﴾ His word, ﴿"and we obey"﴾ His command. ﴿"Your forgiveness"﴾, meaning: "Grant us Your forgiveness."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 2, verse 286:

﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.﴾ We have mentioned that this verse abrogated (naskh) what the believers complained of regarding being called to account for whispered thoughts and the promptings of the soul. ﴿It shall have what it has earned﴾ (of good deeds, through obedience) ﴿and it shall bear what it has earned﴾ (of sin, through disobedience). That is: no one is taken to account for another's sin.

﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task﴾ That is: say this as a teaching in the form of supplication. Its meaning is: do not punish us if we forget. The Children of Israel, when they forgot something of what had been prescribed for them, were hastened into punishment for it, so Allah commanded His Prophet and the believers to ask Him to refrain from taking them to task for that. ﴿Or if we err.﴾ That is, we abandon what is right.

﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden (iṣr)﴾ That is: a weight. The meaning is: do not impose upon us a command that is heavy. ﴿As You laid it upon those before us.﴾ Like what the Children of Israel were commanded of the heavy burdens that were upon them.

﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear.﴾ That is: do not punish us with the Fire. ﴿You are our Mawlā (Protector)﴾, our helper, and the One who manages our affairs. ﴿So give us victory over the disbelieving people.﴾ In establishing our proof and in our prevailing over them in battle and in all their affairs, until Our religion becomes manifest over all religion, as You promised us.
